TL;DR: 9.9/10 (nearly perfect).
Pros: too many to quickly list, see paragraph below.
Cons: steep learning curve, and potential expense of the full (& extremely important) game in the form of tons of DLC.
CK2 has quickly become one of my favourite games of all time. This game is such a fun mix of history/alternate history, intrigue, state/empire building, and ruler simulator. The possibilities available (with all the DLC) are so numerous that during the 400+ hours I’ve played I’ve barely scratched the surface. Wonder what would happen if the Vikings had conquered, held, and integrated Italy into the Swedish or Norwegian kingdoms? DO IT. Getting tired of the Catholics attacking you when you play as the Umayyads (muslim rulers of the Iberian peninsula)? Holy war all the Catholic countries, take their territory and convert their populations to Islam; Rome the center of Catholicism? Not any more! take it from the Infidels and make it Sunni (or Shi'a), or if you're not muslim then convert it to Norse or any of the multitude of diverse and historically accurate religions .  The possibilities for epic, "world" conquering and non-historically accurate shenanigans are nearly infinite.  Let your inner history nerd free, and mess with the world in a fun, engaging, and often very personal way. Another important aspect of this game besides the world conquering/state building is the character aspect.  Instead of just playing a country you are actually an individual (a count, duke, king, or emperor).  Individuals have traits which affect (positively or negatively) their stats which in turn affect the functionality of your state.  There are thousands of unique events for your character to “interact” with, adding an aspect of role playing that is not merely a side thing but a full fledged and fleshed out mechanic.  All the possibilities and outcomes an individual character can experience keeps the game from being just another conquer the enemies territory and “take over the world” (brain) game and elevates it into a unique class of it’s own. There are only two negatives to this game, both of which ultimately don’t affect it's enjoyability. First problem is the price of the game and all it’s DLC. To get the best (and “real”) CK2 experience you really do need all the DLC and when it’s not on sale this game can cost $150+. Lucky the game goes on sale frequently and I’ve been able to (over some time) acquire all the DLC for much, MUCH less than $150. I don’t know exactly how much but it’s probably only like $40/50. Buying the "complete package" at the start when on sale costs $40 and is definitly a perfect deal.  Le'ts just say that despite not paying $150+ for the game I've definitly gotten WAY more than $150 worth of fun from it. I'm glad I didn't pay that much but now that I know how good the game is and if I had to go back & pay the full price I wouldn't hesitate.  The second problem is the learning curve. Being a grand strategy game there is a MASSIVE amount of stuff to learn.  I’m not the sharpest tool in the shed so it took me a good 50+ hours before I was confident enough to say I fully knew how to play. The essential link between Mass Effect and Mass Effect 3.
Mass Effect 2 is less focused on the general story background, but puts building a team and relationships into the focus of its story line. Apart from the introduction of the "Collectors", there's isn't much added to what has been learned about the reapers in Mass Effect 1.
Mass Effect 2 is best enjoyed with an imported save game, giving away bits and pieces about what happened to all the colorful persons the payer met in the first game.
Combat has been drastically simplified, giving way less emphasize on building the character and outfitting them with gear. With speed of the encounters picking up, the tactical impact of squad utilization has been dropped seomwhat in favor of putting the player's reaction time more into focus. It's not necessarily a bad thing, but won't appeal to those who wish for a less hectic approach to combat.
While enjoying ME 2 greatly at the first time, I personally didn't find the second playthrough of ME 2 as rewarding as it felt for ME 1, because of the rather thin story development. While building relationships with the NPCs feels rewarding, it comes somewhat short in terms of depths. Less squad mates with more character development would have been preferable.
Bottom line: Essential to (re)live the trilogy, but feels slightly like a stretch for those who already know about the dramatic developments of ME 3.
PS: Don't miss updating the game with a HD texture modification! Due to technical limitations the developers did include low res textures only! The screenshots I have taken showcase HD textures for all squadmates.

Alright, I won't lie, whenever I see "Free to Play" on Steam I read "Pay to Win", so I knew from the start what to expect and as a matter of fact, that's exactly what I got.
Setting aside the fact that it's more of a mobile game and definitely not something worth porting as a computer game it still is a good time waster. In fact it's even fairly enjoyable for the first couple hours of gameplay.
Progression's smooth, there's a good balance between whatever army you can build (for free) and the campaign difficulty, RNGesus' a ♥♥♥♥♥ but that's something we're all used to... BUT once you get past a certain point it gets more and more difficult to advance without spending money or mindlessly grinding like hell hoping for some good RNG procs.
PVP gets totally unbalanced quickly since buyers gets in the way (A single rank 5 unit which is part of the beginner's package, NOT maxed out, can take down your whole army nearly singlehandedly, warlord included, even though you have 3 times your opponent's level / army value... seriously?) which prevent's you from building up winning streaks, which prevents you from farming energy, a necessery component to upgrade your army / items efficiency. In other words, you NEED it, but you CAN'T get it if you don't pay.
Same goes for evolving your troops; grinding is all well and good as an alternative for smoking your credit card, but if you can't beat the level in which you can get the units you need and not some useless or sub-component grunt, what's the point?
Those are the reasons why I can't recommend this game. If you aim to waste a dozen or so hours it's fine, but don't expect to progress any further without spending something (not necessarily hundreds of bucks, but at least some).

Owlboy:
~~~~~~

Despite the long, hard training given by his mentor, the famous Owl Asio, Owl-hood has not been very easy for a small, mute owl named Otus. His first flight was not one to be remembered, if you ask Asio. The disappointment on Otus’ face could have be seen from miles away. Well, today is another day, thought Otus before taking his watch over the floating Island of Vellie. It’s a big day for an Owlboy like him, especially after reports of pirate ships flying around the area! You know you can do it Owlboy, you know you can!
Owlboy is a platformer / adventure game where you play a small owl, who, with the help of his friends, will have to save the capital Advent from a pirate invasion.
You will be greeted by a fabulous piece of orchestral music as soon as you land on the main menu page; it truly gave me goose bumps!
As you start a new game you will be introduced to the story, which will also include a short tutorial. Then your character will wake up on the floating city of Vellie, where you will receive your first orders. This chapter is pretty much an exploratory one and will give you a good feel of how to manoeuvre your owl, as well as what to look for in each level: coins and heath items.  Most of the coins are half-lodged into the ground - pull them up and coins will appear. You will also earn coins by flying through rings which are scattered all around the levels. There are a certain number of coins to be discovered per stage. If you find them all, you’ll earn a golden star and it will also contribute to accessing special devices from the buccanary’s shop. To restore health, just pick fruits from trees or pull vegetables from the ground.

As you progress through the story and meeting new characters, some of them will join. One point I forgot to mention - Otus doesn’t have weapons! Sure, he can fly, roll and twist his wings but he can’t shoot anything. He carries someone around who can shoot at enemies. Enemies are pretty fun, lion thingies that spit fire from their mouths, cavemen who throw rocks at you, pirates and their parachute explosives and one-eyed flying green balls, to cite a few. Boss fights are quite tricky here and has taken me several attempts to beat some of them so far.
Nice puzzles, however quite obvious in my opinion.

The pixel artwork is fabulous and I really like the fluidity of the animations. The soundtrack is splendid - it grabs you from the start. Control-wise, you can use the mouse and keyboard but I prefer to use a gamepad – it’s better, in my opinion. It is quite easy to go through the levels, apart from the boss fights, which are more challenging.
Positives:
~~~~~~~
-	Great graphics and animations
-	Splendid soundtrack
-	Responsive controls
-	Good story and characters
-	Achievements and trading cards
Negatives:
~~~~~~~~
-	Needed to be more challenging
Owlboy is a very well-designed game with splendid pixel artwork, great animations and marvellous music!
9/10

I'm writing this review immediately after completing the game.
Owlboy is a very solid Metroidvania-style platformer with a heavy focus on flying. The game's developer drew inspiration from Mario's Tanooki suit (the flying squirrel/cat-looking thing), so you spend a lot of time gliding through the air as you traverse the different areas of the map.
The whole map in Owlboy is connected (similar to Legend of Zelda) and there is generally no teleporting between areas or individual, World 1-1, 1-2, etc.-style levels, like in some Mario games.
The visual design of this game is incredible. Though the graphics are outdated by today's standards, you can tell the devs put a ton of love and care into their 16-bit artwork. Islands float through the air in the background, shrubs blow in the wind, and enemies move naturally. The sound design is just as good, with a memorable soundtrack that captures the mood of the moment nicely.
The plot of Owlboy is interesting, though a bit cliche. However, I grew to love the characters and their individual personalities pretty early. Don't expect to really be surprised too much by any of the plot twists, though.
My first playthrough (blind) took me roughly 8 hours. After completing the game, there is little to do, aside from collect the remaining coins throughout the game (if you're a completionist). You may be thinking, "Ok, an 8-hour game for $25. Seems pretty steep." And you may be right. I paid roughly $16 for the game during a sale and I'm 100% pleased with my purchase.
If $25 is too much for you, wait for a sale/price drop. Owlboy is an outstanding retro-style platformer with a charming cast of characters, wonderful visuals, and a fantastic soundtrack. Flying becomes snappy (after the first couple hours of playing and mastering it - learning things, such as how to fly just a bit faster and whatnot) and there is really only one poorly-designed/frustrating area (detailed below). Overall, I give Owlboy a 9/10. Buy it if you're interested and have the cash.
-----------------------------------------------
Frustrating area: There's a section where you have to do a pretty long, Indiana-Jones style escape from a collapsing cave. Problem is, it's pretty much entirely based upon you remembering when and where to do stuff. You have a small margin of error, so any mistake results in death. Additionally, using the wrong character could instantly ruin your run since you need to use a specific ability at an exact time and if you don't have it off cooldown - you die.
This area isn't really the issue. The main problem comes from the fact that upon dying, you have to activate a screw, which takes about 10 seconds, and wait for a 5-second cutscene before trying again. Skilled players will only have to do this a few times, but I got stuck here and attempted this section of the game about 30 times. As a result, I got very frustrated screwing the stupid screw into the ground, waiting for the cutscene to play and then finally getting to try again. Just this "waiting" section before the escape took about 8 total minutes of time. I was so ready to be finished with this area.
Once you FINALLY beat the Indiana Jones escape part, there is an immediate boss fight, followed by another pretty difficult two-part escape section. The second escape section, similar to the first one, has no checkpoints, requiring you to finish both parts without dying. This section of the game, in my opinion, is by far the weakest. It's only about 5-10 minutes of gameplay (if you finish the escape, boss fight and second escape in a single attempt) and shouldn't keep you from buying the game. However, this area seemed poorly thought out and was the only part of the game that I didn't particularly enjoy.
EDIT: Upon further reflection, I found the "final boss" battle to be quite underwhelming. I beat it the first try. Also, I'm sad that I never got to fight a certain villain, in particular. That also really sucks. Owlboy is still a wonderful game.

There IS a surprise twist to the story, but it takes a lot of jumping through hoops, trial, and error to get it. The translation from Japanese to English also fails in many places, and while it's the most entertaining thing about this game, sadly, it doesn't save it from all its cons.
It's a shame, because the ending IS good, but having to repeat a lot of endings and steps just to get the true one just isn't fun, and doesn't make it worthwhile.

Huh... it's hard to recommend Return NULL. It doesn't do anything badly, per se, but there's nothing to recommend it as a game, really.
It's basically a very limited, linear, plot driven comic book. And a really, really short one.
While the writting isn't all that bad, this is completely unfit for a game. You have no agency at all. There are some dialogue choices, but they don't seem to change anything. It's all an illusion of choice, while you get the same result regardless.
I don't like plot-driven media in general, so your opinion may be very different from mine.
But here's the thing. This game is a big setup. They try to have some emotional impact in the beginning, but mostly fail, since you have about 2 minutes to make the emotional bond. Too fast and in your face to achieve anything, personally.
Then, they try to present the world and its dystopian issues, but it barely has any content for it to work. There's no exploration, no talking to interesting characters... everything is placed to move the plot forward. And the plot isn't any good either. It may become good, but it's a 30-40 minutes game, at most. And a big part of that is walking back and forth, so it's not really a good measure.
The images are static as well. The game is gorgeous. I really like the look of it. But... it would look just as good as a comic book.
Only, it would have more pictures...
The music is alright as well, and sets the mood correctly.
No interesting puzzles, no interesting characters, no exploration, nothing. There's absolutely nothing that makes this benefit as game. It only hurts it, honestly. Because it creates situations for the player to "interact", i.e. use screwdriver to open something, or use piers to cut wires... They don't add anything to the game, they're simply there, making things clunky.
Yeah, not a fan at all. It's not broken or anything, it's pretty solid at what it does. It's just that what it does is not much.

I didn't know what kind of game I was running into, pictures and description didn't help much understanding how really is the game, so I wasn't sure I would enjoy this one. Luckily I was surprised, in a  good way of course.
You are Ronan a detective with a troubled past. Small crimes, jail, reformed as a cop, married with Julia, widow. All of this to make you understand what kind of guy this Ronan is: rash. So this is how the story begins, with Ronan's death as he broke alone into an apartment where the Bell Killer has been sighted. Once he died by the Killer's hand, Ronan (now a ghost) has to solve his pending business in this realm in order to ascend and find peace with Julia. And here we are, in Salem, our own town trying to solve our own murder and the Bell Killer's case.
Developed with Unreal Engine the game shows a respectable level of details, though somehow seems like it hasn't been fully optimized as it runs fine almost all the time on my system but there are some minor slowdowns here and there. Another downnote lies in the artistic aspect of the city and ambients. Even though it's fine to see the entire city to be dark and with black and blue tones except for the church (subtle but coherent and appreciated) as we are dead, I believe the game is excessively dark, I had to enhance brightness from the game menu a bit too much making the game looking a bit unnatural now. Ambiences should have been lightened in a more balanced way to prevent this.
Nothing outstanding captured my attention so I guess nothing bad but nothing good. They mostly consists of vibed strings, a classic heard in many horrors in scary or ominous moments. However voice acting is generally good and convincing.
Murdered: Soul Suspect is an investigation game, so that's what you will do. With all the implications of being a ghost, of course, so you can walk through most of the walls, you can possess living people to read their mind or to influence them to do certain actions or to think about certain events.
Anyways, The investigation takes place in every single "crime scene" you will have to analyze: look for clues around this place, then pick up the right clues that better help the main character answering his questions. This is the core of the gameplay, but this is not everything you can do as you have to walk around the small town of Salem from one place to another, you will have to talk with other characters (often ghosts), there are collectibles that tell stories of other cases, or personal stories, there are other ghosts that need your help (hence other investigation, call them secondary quests if you wish).
Wandering around the town however doesn't mean you are a ghost in Los Santos. This is not an Open World game, you can't walk through every building or house you want (a simple yet effective reason for this is explained in the first moments of the game). So do not expect any of that.

Do you want this game?
Reasons you want this game:
+ Unique crime-solving detective gameplay
+ Numerous collectibles to gather & areas to explore
+ Open world game: once you unlock a zone, you can access them at any time and run around on your own accord
+ Each zone has unique interactable items, collectibles, and gameplay
+ You can play as a cat
+ An interesting take on a ghost story, where you play as the ghost and not the living person
+ The game is driven by its story
+ Unlock new powers as you complete each chapter of the game
Reasons you DON'T want this game:
- The game is short and expensive. Many will say they can't stop playing the game, and chances are they will finish it in one sitting, like me
- Aside from the main story, not much to do. There are collectibles and side quests, but there is no impact on the game, not even cosmetics
Some small notes on the game:
~ Demons don't belong in the game. They are nothing but a roadblock that you have to sneak up on and kill with a QTE
~ There were many chances to make the game longer, and it honestly should have been. The average player will complete the ENTIRE game in 11 hours (100% Steam achievements)
~ Judging by the release date, they most likely wanted to capitalize on the "older male protagonist, young female sidekick," as it was a trend at the time
~ Some of the detective gameplay is odd. Example: what would make the suspect think of the killer? Answer: The killer. That's extremely obvious and pointless
~ The characters are written almost one-dimensionally. No character has more than maybe one definable trait, and can only be told apart by their fashion sense
~ The story is okay but won't blow your socks off. Almost certain it has been done many times before
VERDICT:
The game has a lot to improve on in my eyes. The gameplay is alright, but everything else needs a bit of a pick-me-up. Aesthetically the game looks great, and controls are pretty solid too. I don't believe I encountered a single bug or glitch either, which is a huge plus in my books. Overall, I wish the game was longer, and that any side quests, stories, and collectibles did more for the gameplay and wasn't just an easter egg hunt into nothing. I like seeing cosmetic change, or story-altering decisions when it comes to quests, helping people, and collecting everything possible, but it just doesn't  happen. The game can be bought, downloaded, played, beat, and put away all in one sitting; We are talking about maybe 6 hours to beat the game, and 11 to do everything possible. Could they make a part two? I really don't think so, it wasn't a good enough story or universe to warrant it. Maybe DLC, but it's far too late now. This is a good one if you're someone who prefers a multitude of genre elements (in this case, a little bit of crime drama, fantasy, horror), rather than one big single genre game.
This review was written only after completing the game to it's fullest, 100% capacity. I try to accomplish this task before having any formal opinions on any games I review.

DreadOut is a low-budget survival horror debut made by studio Digital Happiness. The story revolves around a school trip that erroneously bumps into a ghost town which they have the urge to explore. I don't think there's more needed to say, overall it feels (with poor voice acting) like an average B movie. Just to keep the feel of location, besides many locked doors, you'll be actually finding notes with backstory of specific places.
Backstory might help you getting more into the game, but what's the main feature of DreadOut, is the brilliant horror atmosphere. Scary sounds that you can't recognize, creepy environment with well designed ghosts, jumpscares and ubiquitous darkness is something the game does in a great way. But that applies to the horror segments, that has more or less boring walking around itself.
All gameplay mechanisms are bound to smartphone of the protagonist, Linda. With your everlasting battery, you'll use your phone as a flashlight and a camera. Puzzles use camera flashes or peeking through it, as you might see different things through the camera. The everlasting battery for flashlight is compensated with the fact that you may not want to be using it all the time, there might be a situations where you'll rather decide to spend your time in the dark that may feel somehow safer.
Level design has enough room for you to get lost; there are situations where you might not be sure what to do next. Developers tried to help you at least a little, as they added Linda's diary into the game where you can always check your current objective. There isn't any proper tutorial in the game but all controls and gameplay mechanics are explained in the "how to play" section of the menu. I don't think of horror game players as casuals, so I think it shouldn't be a problem for anybody interested.
I tried to be positive with the game as far, but it's time to mention the bad things. DreadOut is not for everybody, I understand why it feels great for experienced horror game players, but I found the gameplay overall more boring that I'd originally expect. Making all the gameplay around walking and using camera seems to be a good idea, but personally it didn't feel much satisfying to me after about an hour. While the short game length can't even make it much repetitive, you still might lose a motivation to continue - the only "magnet" there is truly the atmosphere.
Graphics are something that can make players ask themselves if they are really playing a game released in 2014. While the ghosts look great and characters look somehow fine, the environment around you, when not placed into darkness, looks really bad. Many objects and their textures reminded me of Counter-Strike 1.6 and basic 3D graphics modeling - For example, I haven't seen cars that would look like "slightly better boxes with textures" for a really long time.
Oh, and you'll be able to see through some walls with third-person camera. Another nail in the coffin is the bad optimalisation that even with the poor graphics sucks up performance pretty badly. Don't expect getting high with your FPS counter.
While DreadOut does a great things in terms of the horror atmosphere, the other factors are making the experience for worse, mostly. It's definitely not a game for everybody, and considering it doesn't offer even many hours of gameplay to those who don't want to unlock all achievements, I don't think it's worth recommending.
My copy of DreadOut was obtained for free - I won the game in a giveaway that might have been sponsored by the developer. This fact hasn't changed my opinion about the game (and the review) in any way.

Crysis Warhead, technically a sequel to the original Crysis, you play as Psycho, a teammate of Nomad (the main character in the first game). At some point in the original Crysis, you two split up to handle separate missions, this game takes place right after that and ends right before you meet back up in the original, thus, it is a fairly short game.
Story: 8/10
Because it is in the same time-frame and environment as the original Crysis, not much needs to be explained. You already know what is going on, but at some points it felt kind of cheesy and forced, and you are also following this damned container that remains ever out of reach until the very end. Not a BAD story, besides, you are playing this for the fun of messing around most likely.
Graphics and Audio: 9/10
Despite a few points in the game where my framerate choked out, Crytek did a marvelous job with this game in terms of graphics. This game came out approximately a year after the original, which means they optimized their code and this didn't make my computer want to cry. It runs smoother and looks cleaner, and is completely action-packed from the get-go. Also, the cut scenes are in third person, which I feel is an improvement so you can see how your character is reacting to his situation as it develops. As far as audio, it sounds about the same quality as the original Crysis so all is good in this department.
Gameplay: 8/10
Same game as Crysis, but in my personal opinion, I had more fun before the aliens show up. I was looking forward to sneaking around and messing with my Korean enemies, and because this game starts so close to when all hell breaks loose, you don't really get a chance to do that. That aside, however, the controls feel really familiar and smooth, I was going to play with my Xbox controller but when it comes to FPS games, I prefer keyboard and mouse. By the way, the game is Gamepad enabled if you want it to be.
Overall: 9/10
It isn't the original Crysis, and that isn't necessarily BAD. The game is shorter and plays MUCH smoother, but I feel that the story in the original was slightly better. Both games are great and I recommend buying both. The game excels at showing what Crytek does really well, creating an action-packed blockbuster movie, but instead of the movie, it is a game, which is amazing.
Additionally, this game comes with Crysis Wars, apparently a Multiplayer Crysis, I didn't try it, have no interest.

First of all, this is a beautiful game, has a lot.. and I mean a LOT of content and is actually can be potentially fun.
and here.. we'll start with the positives:
The graphics are superb for an MMO, truly does the CryEngine justice.
Player housing.
Classes for any playstyle with a unique method of selection.
Open world PVP done in a way where you know it's coming.
Full scale wars.
Doing anything.. from being just a farmer, to a pirate.. anything is possible.
Ships.. SHIPS! you can finally set sail in an MMO and have epic battles!
So much more that I can't even think of right now!
So... yeah.. those trailers.. they don't lie... you can do everything seen in the trailers yourself...
Well.. there's the "But... dude.. if it sounds so awesome, then why don't you recommend it?"
There's 2 reasons.. 2 reasons that ruin the entire game for me.
1. Labor System
2. Time Needed
As I put it, it's "potentially fun" it has so much going for it, but it has a limited labor system, you've got to stay logged in to get "labor Points" every 5 minutes, which can easily be wasted in a couple minutes if you're not careful. With that said, there's a way to get around without wasting so much labor and that is focus. When you focus on doing a single thing (for example, mining, then selling raw materials), you can stretch your in-game labor and end up doing so much more with planning, but that's not always how things end up, especially when you want to try new things, you just can't very easily without doing nothing and waiting for labor points, or spending your hard earned gold to get more.
Okay, this one may be more of a personal thing, but it's not hard to see, from the labor system alone, that this is a time sink, you can't leave it running In the background to earn labor and render something in your favorite 3D software (like 3DS MAX for example... and yes, I've tried). That last statement is a pretty limited one and is more of a personal issue, but, the game is also quite tedious, everything takes a while, so when you look at your clock, you'll look at it what feels like 5 minutes later and realize it's been 3 hours and you're still on the same beach as before, doing the same thing over and over again. I mean... come on.. I know it's fun to feel like you've achieved something by working hard.. but.. it's a game.. working TOO hard can drive players away.
also: and end note.. for those thinking about it.. I would recommend getting Ascension packs from Trion instead of Steam if you don't like the idea of somehow not getting the packs.

At the time of writing this review I have nearly 200 hours invested into this game. Please understand, this does not happen. I'm the kind of guy who MIGHT get a dozen hours out of a single-player game, MAYBE 30 if it's an RPG.  But to think that I can get 200 hours or more out of a single-player game is crazy. So what is it about this game?
1: The history.  If you are even considering this game you must have some interest in history.  Most people, including myself, didn't know much about the middle ages other than castles, knights, and christians killing muslims killing christians.  But Crusader Kings II shows you so much more: There are the Vikings to the north, the Picts in what would become Scotland, there are Leon, Castile, Aragon, and other minor kingdoms that would someday become Spain, the Muslim presence on the Iberian Peninsula, the Orthodox Byzantines facing Catholics on one side and Muslims on the other, even the Indian kingdoms that existed during that period.
2: The alternate history.  This is definitely the biggest selling point.  Sure, you could start as a duke in the British Isles, form the kingdom of England, and then just duke it out with France for the next 400 years. Or, you could go out and conquer the entirety of Catholic Europe, assimilate the Germanic Saxons and Norse, show the Byzantines the error of their ways (with the pointy end of your sword) crusade against the heathen Muslims and even take India for good measure.  So much detail has gone into the potential for kingdoms that were just a mino blip on history's radar.  You can play as the Byzantines and reform the Roman Empire as well are re-unite the two branches of Christianity.  You can have a Jewish ruler who re-conquers Jerusalem, re-forms the Kingdom of Israel, and rebuilds the Temple of Solomon to usher in a golden age of prosperity for the Jewish people. You can even reform a pagan religion such as Germanic to bring it on par with the mainstream monotheistic religions.
3. The variation.  You will never see the AI play two games the same way.  Take France for example.  In the Charlemagne starting point, France starts split into two kingdoms, Western Francia and Middle Francia. In some games, the two empires will merge to form the Empire of Francia.  Other times, They will combine with Italy to form the Holy Roman Empire. And still others, they will be wracked with so many rebellions that they will splinter into a half-dozen smaller kingdoms.  Likewise, the Byzantines or the Abbasids (the major Muslim power) can expand and expand and expand, or fall apart at the seams. The game has endless playability because you CAN NOT play the same game twice.
Now, if you're still considering whether to get this game, understand that you will EASILY invest 50 or more hours before even getting a grip on the basics. As of writing this, I just had to restart a game I played for 20 hours easlily because of a bad choice in when to turn from tribal government to feudalism.  But I'm still learning about the game, even with 200 hours. I've sat in this chair for 12 hours straight at times, that's how good this game is. But understand that it is quite a hefty time investment, it's not something you can play for 15 or 20 minute sittings.

You play as Michael "Psycho" Sykes working on another set of mission on the other side of the island. You're more impulsive, so the missions are more suitable for an aggressive play style. You can still try to use stealth if you like though.
Some of the more memorable moments:
1. You chase down the Korean General in a Hovercraft over a frozen jungle, while epic music play in the background.
2. You hijack a train with mounted Heavy Machineguns and Automatic Grenade Launchers while human and alien enemies try to take you down.
3. You fight off enemies across an entire airfield, only to realize when you've cleared the Korean troops, it's overran by aliens. There is also epic music in the background, in case you're wondering.
The major complaint about this game is the unpolished cutscenes: there's no voice dialogue (even when Psycho is being tortured, he doesn't even grunt, although his face is clearly in agony). People say nothing, so you're watching these silent cutscenes with occasional ambient sounds. They felt really awkward, like they were added in last minute.
In any case, great fun for a short campaign.

This platformer feels different from more traditional platformers.
Sometimes, this gap from the expected hurts the game.
For example, the player is introduced to the capitol city via its ugly bottom—it feels more like a single building than the vast city it means to represent. Later, two different panoramas of the city are shown. Why, then, weren't one of those beautiful backgrounds used to introduce the city?
Level design is not intuitive. You'll often loop back around the same level. Swapping from traditional platformer to a sort of stealth mode or a jumping puzzle or a sidescroller or a gauntlet is often jarring, but this spontaneity has its advantages. The unexpected can be exciting and new—some of the puzzles in this game I've never encountered before in any platformer I've done.
There's no clear physical progression, which makes the end come rather unexpectedly. New moves are not unlocked as the player plays, and neither does difficulty ramp up over the course of the game (the hardest part, for me, was a boss fight somewhere in the game's middle). The closest a first-time player might come to understanding their in-game progress is probably from looking at the number of trinkets they've collected, of which there are a clear and finite number.
Developers clearly had an overarching story in mind, and where that overlaps with the story that is actually told is apparent, because in those cases, the game's story feels impressive and players might feel engaged in it. The story that is actually played through, however, is incredibly confusing, full of false-starts and switchbacks and entirely too much falling action. The story sometimes cops out on explaining how the player gets from one place to another (apparently the snow level is about a minute's walk from the jungle level).
Despite not being a traditional platformer, and despite how dearly this game screams to be optimized for user-friendliness, this game is good thanks to its unique feel, its top-quality aesthetics, and its epic ending.

I don't feel chapter 1 was worth paying for on its own purely because it is so incredibly short.
More detail:
Return NULL has a few things that are very promising. The writers have created a dystopian future world that is, initially at least, interesting and a main character with some depth and a back story that makes you want to know more. From playing the first episode I really, really hope that this develops into a full blown well written science fiction story.
However the first chapter feels more like a taster than a proper first chapter to a game. It's not even as much as some games offer as a free demo. I think comments about the low budget sound and visuals are a little unfair given the cost of the game but if the developers want us to believe that this is a story worth hearing, they should have given us a a bit more detail. This could have been in the form of more characters to interact with,  a few more locations to explore, or a few more puzzles.
I really hope that when the developers get the funds they will make a more substantial chapter 2 but I'm not holding my breath.

Pros:
* compelling story with interesting plot twists
* nicely dark mood, with a tinge of noir
* potential for interesting mechanics
* a few of interesting side quests (though some of them were pathetically bland and random)
* a couple of funny ghost encounters + ghost stories were a nice-ish touch
* not too long (I'm looking at you AC, TES and Witcher ;p )
Cons:
* Awkward, artificial-feeling, mood-spoiling ghost game-mechanics (e.g. movement limitations)
* Even more awkward and very artificial "arcade" elements (demons)
* Extremely repetitive "investigation" parts
* somewhat less believable protagonist
* might be considered short-ish by some
All in all, I don't consider this game to be a _bad_ game... it's not... but it just cannot be called a good game either... As someone said "it's the worst game I enjoyed playing" and I feel there's much truth in this description. If it wasn't for the overwhelming artificiality of the movement and the somewhat frustrating and unconvincing fight/stealth parts, I might even actually lean towards "Recommend" end of spectrum... As it is though, I think the only good part of the game is the mood and the story... So - were this a novella - or an indie movie maybe - I might even be convinced I watched some cool "cult-ish" noir flick or read a nifty little thriller... but this being a game with such awkward, unconvincing/repetitive mechanics and at the same time one that really _seems_ like a really good game judging by the cover, I would say, no, I can't honestly recommend it...

When I first saw the reveal trailer for this game, I was rather underwhelmed, that is, until the main character died within the first minute of gameplay! To say I was intrigued was an understatement.
Ever since I was a wee lad, I had a deep-rooted interest in ghosts, goblins and other beings that go bump in the night. I remember watching documentaries on supposedly haunted buildings from the safety of my covers and jumping at the shadows that danced across my walls from passed cars outside. In particular, I remember watching a tape of a one-off special called “Haunted Lighthouses” back in 1998 during Halloween and despite not having watched it in the 19 years since I lost the tape, I still recall it’s foreboding atmosphere and dire stories of horror like it was yesterday.
While my interest has waned since then, Murdered : Soul Suspect pretty much brought my child-like fascination back from the dead with it’s thick atmosphere and eerie setting in perhaps one of the most recognizable towns in Americana Folklore!
The game starts shortly after the death of our main character, who, much like in life, is tasked with solving a murder. However, now it is his own murder!
I quickly grew to like the main lead and many of the characters that followed, coupled with surprisingly engaging writing and pacing made the games narrative stand out among other narrative-driven experiences in recent memory.
The more I played, the more I fell in love with the mystery-driven situations. You’ll have to scour rooms for evidence, even using supernatural powers to reveal clues that no living detective could feasibly find, such as revealing past memories or phasing through solid walls. Hunting for clues immediately gave me flashbacks to LA Noire and while it is nowhere near as in-depth or as detailed, it is still an engaging gameplay element that helped hook me into the lore of the world and gave me the drive to follow the story to it’s conclusion!
However, as good as the narrative drew me in and the setting captivated me like a 7 year old child peering over his shoulder for nefarious specters, the combat sadly falls very flat.
Many times throughout the game, our main lead is confronted by demons and lost souls, which sadly, cannot be harmed directly. This turns the game into an unnecessary stealth game and brings the pacing of the narrative to a screeching halt. They themselves are far from hard and defeating them from behind just feels like a grind. And once they spot you, it turns into a frustrating game of cat and mouse until you wait for them to calm down and resume their aggravating patrols once more. The game could have certainly benefited from a legitimate combat system and the stealth elements would be better off left in the trash bin.
Another aspect that fell to the sideline was the rating system! It wasn’t until halfway did I start to notice that failed prompts in certain cases had ZERO consequences, beyond just a meaningless rating for the investigation that earns no benefits or repercussions for coming to the wrong conclusion. In LA Noire, this would have led to the player losing evidence or even outright failing a case!
Waltzing through the town of Salem, while alluring and oozing mystery at first, suddenly felt cramped and unfinished! Many times I would come across a spirit who honestly feels like he or she had an intended quest, only to trade a couple of lines of dialogue before turning away disinterested.
Regardless, I still came away from this game satisfied with the story and narrative. It’s certainly not for everyone, especially those looking for in-depth combat and other gameplay, but for someone like me, it was a flawed yet delightful treat! Given it’s relatively short length (I myself spent a good portion of my 21 hours scouring for collectibles and leaving the game running in the background) and artificial difficulty, it’s certainly a far-cry to demand a purchase given it’s current price, but I would certainly recommend picking this up if it goes on sale!

TL;DR: 9.9/10 (nearly perfect).
Pros: too many to quickly list, see paragraph below.
Cons: steep learning curve, and potential expense of the full (& extremely important) game in the form of tons of DLC.
CK2 has quickly become one of my favourite games of all time. This game is such a fun mix of history/alternate history, intrigue, state/empire building, and ruler simulator. The possibilities available (with all the DLC) are so numerous that during the 400+ hours I’ve played I’ve barely scratched the surface. Wonder what would happen if the Vikings had conquered, held, and integrated Italy into the Swedish or Norwegian kingdoms? DO IT. Getting tired of the Catholics attacking you when you play as the Umayyads (muslim rulers of the Iberian peninsula)? Holy war all the Catholic countries, take their territory and convert their populations to Islam; Rome the center of Catholicism? Not any more! take it from the Infidels and make it Sunni (or Shi'a), or if you're not muslim then convert it to Norse or any of the multitude of diverse and historically accurate religions .  The possibilities for epic, "world" conquering and non-historically accurate shenanigans are nearly infinite.  Let your inner history nerd free, and mess with the world in a fun, engaging, and often very personal way. Another important aspect of this game besides the world conquering/state building is the character aspect.  Instead of just playing a country you are actually an individual (a count, duke, king, or emperor).  Individuals have traits which affect (positively or negatively) their stats which in turn affect the functionality of your state.  There are thousands of unique events for your character to “interact” with, adding an aspect of role playing that is not merely a side thing but a full fledged and fleshed out mechanic.  All the possibilities and outcomes an individual character can experience keeps the game from being just another conquer the enemies territory and “take over the world” (brain) game and elevates it into a unique class of it’s own. There are only two negatives to this game, both of which ultimately don’t affect it's enjoyability. First problem is the price of the game and all it’s DLC. To get the best (and “real”) CK2 experience you really do need all the DLC and when it’s not on sale this game can cost $150+. Lucky the game goes on sale frequently and I’ve been able to (over some time) acquire all the DLC for much, MUCH less than $150. I don’t know exactly how much but it’s probably only like $40/50. Buying the "complete package" at the start when on sale costs $40 and is definitly a perfect deal.  Le'ts just say that despite not paying $150+ for the game I've definitly gotten WAY more than $150 worth of fun from it. I'm glad I didn't pay that much but now that I know how good the game is and if I had to go back & pay the full price I wouldn't hesitate.  The second problem is the learning curve. Being a grand strategy game there is a MASSIVE amount of stuff to learn.  I’m not the sharpest tool in the shed so it took me a good 50+ hours before I was confident enough to say I fully knew how to play.  The 50ish hours I spent learning were fun but I didn’t realize how amazing this game is until I actually got fluent in the game (around 100+ hours in).  Now though that i’ve “mastered” how the game is played I struggle to name a game I’ve enjoyed playing more (ok I know: The Binding of Isaac/Rebirth).  One way to help speed up learning the ins & outs is to watch tutorial/let’s play videos. There is a youtuber named Arumba who is not only extremely entertaining but is also a CK2 master.  Watching his CK2 content really helped accelerate my enjoyment and understanding of the game. I fully recommend watching some tutorial/let’s play videos while/before playing the game, it’ll help alleviate some of the frustration/insurmountability and intimidation the first time you boot CK2 up.  I can’t recommend this game strongly enough, it is gigatons of fun. I also recommend Arumba if you like LP’s and funny/entertaining yet not idiotic/spas-tic presenters then Arumba should be topping your list of ppl to watch. (FYI: I have no affiliation w/ Arumba nor do I know him, I’m just a fan making a recommendation)

"DreadOut" is a third person horror-game and was published in May 2014.
I came to the conclusion that I can't recommend DreadOut - even though  the game features a very original story which is based on indonesian folklore and pretty unique mechanics, such as the use of a camera in first person to fend off the ghosts that haunt you during the game. The games story and implementation of ghosts is very well done, the ghosts design is disturbing (as it should be) the story is catchy enough to keep on playing and the concept of photographing ghosts to kill them (plus needing different tactics to kill some of the ghosts) is pretty interesting to me! Even the graphics are "okay", although certainly not on the level of 2014.  Yet the downsides overshadow those positive aspects of the game - if you'd ask me... There are 3 things in particular that annoyed me during the time I played DreadOut: First - The game didn't really scare, but instead startle me with an overabundance of jumpscares... I didn't get a feeling of constant dread while I played, and after a while those jumpscares just annoyed me instead of scaring me... The second thing that bothered me where the boss-fights... those really had the potential to be challenging, yet fair and rewarding as well, but to me they became constant struggles to "not get stuck or stunlocked" under a boss... The last thing which really felt unnecessary and not well-implemented was the "gameover and respawning-process"... To inform you: If you die, which frequently happens, you'll respawn in a black field with a bright light in front of you to which you must walk. Upon every death the distance to said light becomes further and if you die a couple of times (like I did at some harder fights) this process becomes quite frustrating... The distance can be shortend by finding special objects and relics which are scattered throughout the game or by progressing in the story, but if you keep dying to a boss this becomes impossible and thus VERY frustrating...
tl; dnr? Games background and story are good, most of the gameplay sadly isn't! Buy it on sale if you REALLY want to play it, but don't approach it with high expectations...

I originally bought this game as a hard copy so my steam account hasn't logged the probable 100+ hours of game-play I've had from this game.
A fan of the old Command & Conquer games, this appealed and did not disappoint at all.
Firstly, the game play can be picked up very easily and the campaigns are a great way to get to handle the more in depth details as you play through the game and also the factions.
This game, however, came into it's own with the Skirmish option. Single player is always fun to pass the time and release stress by pummelling several opponents into dust. BUT for maximum enjoyment definitely has to be multi-player.
Once my friends and I hooked this up through a network (internet also) say goodbye to a decent nights sleep. The battles were epic, the scale was huge and most games started out as build a HUGE army and just slaughter your friends.
This does get a little overpowered at times but with the options to ban certain units/grades, etc. Then the battles became more interesting.
A friend would attack, you'd figure out a good line of defence, they go back and try work around that defence, you attack your way, they figure out another defence, etc... it was♥♥♥♥♥for tat battle that kept your ideas and strategies rotating and constantly developing.
In the years I've owned this game, it's never lost it's appeal. The graphics are nice & finely detailed, controls are very easy and bulk unit commands are simple, way points & patrols are easy to set. All in all a great strategy game BUT I'd highly recommend multi-player for a long lasting experience.

Read this before you continue!
For me it feels natural to pay a monthly subscription fee and in my opinion you farm for that apex to get your patron (Trion's nick for subscription) or you pay 12,99€ / month. This will give you a fair amount of benefits, including the option to own your own piece of land as well as regenerating labor faster!
I am a former WoW player, played it for 11years. So I will compare those two to some extent.
Keep in mind that I pay every month for my patron benefits(12,99€/month), if you plan on being a F2PP, parts of this review might not be for you.
Yes, it can be annoying for many people. Personally, I like the idea of labor points. It limits the amount of things you can do per day, which adds FUN! You actually (for once in a video game) have to plan, in detail, what you're gonna do when you get online. Perhaps you make trade packs on monday, on tuesday you decide to deliver them and get your gold/resources/gilda stars. Maybe you choose to craft those pieces of armor you have grinded mats for and what not. For me this give me that good feeling that I have achieved something (even though it's just a video game)
Nowadays you also get rewarded various labor pots, up to a max of 1000LP in various chests you're given for free when you reach x lvl, login every day for x amount of days etc.
Conclusion: Planning, work for your items, the feeling of achieving that sweet, sweet item you've been drooling over.
Cash shop, where do I begin. I both like and dislike it, being fairly casual like me I like the fact that instead of dumping my labor on crafting tax certifcates I can buy 5x for 45 credits. I like that, also like that I can buy am expansion scroll for 300 credits instead of spending ~160g buying one @ the auction house. What I dislike is the fact that soooo many people assume that others buy items for thousands of credits day and night to sell @ the auction house only to gain gold to get the "best" gear in no-time.
I have no proof of this but I THINK that this is really not the case with the cash shop,I think there is a couple of people who do this ofc, but they are a minority. I have personally met a bunch of people who haven't spent a cent (not even for the subscription, which can also be bought for credits = Apex) on this game yet they have 5-6k gear score.
Conclusion: Perfect for casual players who feel they can spend a few € here and there, it is a hobby afterall. Can be game-breaking for the people who feel the need to be the top player, this is not the olympics, this is a game. You're supposed to have FUN.
The PvE part of the game is, I would say decent! There are raids, dungeons and world bosses, not as many as in WoW but I did not expect that either since I haven't paid for this title. There are a LOT of daily quests which are entertaining even though I have done them probably too many times, I especially love the "Kill 15 sea bugs / jelly fish" daily, because that means I will spend time on the open sea :)
Also want to count in the owning land part of the game in the PvE section, this part is fantastic. Work your farm, plant those trees and watch them grow, feed your damn hens and what not. Relaxing and fun even though it can be repetitive.
Cannot really give any info on the main story, I rarely spend time on the story in most games I play.
Conlusion: Decent scripting in raids/dungeons, a ton of quests everywhere, I have read that the main story is not triple A material.
Love it! Reminds me of vanilla WoW. You can spank a player in no-time if you have the gear for it. You can also get spanked in no-time, in both cases I usually laugh, because the a$$kicking is real and I say it again, I LOVE IT!
There are pure pvp zones, pvp zones with peace time and naval pvp.
This part of the game is one of reasons for why we have partially toxic community, some people can't stand the fact that people have 1-2k more GS than them. This is a struggle in all mmos, jealousy can bring out the devil in every man or woman.
Conclusion: Easy to kill, easy to get killed, boats.. with cannons.. a massive ocean. Don't need to say anymore on that :) , jealous people hating on geared people = toxic community. This is where the p2w part comes in. If you have mad gear people will say you have no life and spent all your parents money on the game. I choose to ignore this part because the game is too fun to quit because of this reason.

This is also one of the reason people hate on the game, the RNG is a nightmare for many, a breeze for others. It all comes down to how lucky you are. This is for me a thrill, will I make it or will it throw me back out there and farm more gold so I can regrade again. This is too much to write here, search google about info on how regrading works.
Conclusion: While it can get tedious failing over n over it is also a thrill if you gonna make it or not.

Have fun everyone, this game is one of a kind.

TLDR: Is good RPG/Tactical game; you should buy.
I don't review often, just not my thing but for Lord Larian I shall. Played the early access 4 times solo, each time having more fun then the last. Decided to play early access a few times with some friends and had a total blast and some serious laughs. Now at release and loving every second.
RPG elements are excellent and have consequences such as being so much of a scumbag we got a villain tag that unlocked some awesome new dialogues. The world shows clear signs of love and depth, have never had a moment that shocked me out of that all important immersion. Dialog, story and lore are compelling and have me hooked. Game is also fully voiced and is incredibly well done with only a lack of varied accents.(In my opinion) If you like RPG or are a D20 player looking for a good game, this is your winner.
Combat mechanics are tight with some few little knit picks such as ocasionally inaccurate AOE/LOS markers for skills that cause some mistakes that are inevitable with such varied terrain and not game ending. Tactician difficulty is tough but fair, requiring you to turn every battle to your advantage, sometimes even striking an enemy first while a party member distracts them with friendly words. Meanwhile lower difficulties allow for bizarre character combos being viable. The evolving battlefield is fun but requires you to think really hard about every spell you fling. The AI is also ridiculously smart, they know everything about your character except the arsenal you wield. Having spells, abilities, bombs, scrolls and arrows means the only time you cannot to anything is a result of your mismanagement of resources. Only real qualm is resistances existing only for magic as a second line of defence while armour only has dodge and hp. Certain enemies being immune/resistant/absorbing to damage types is interesting while physical only has to deal with dodge.
General mechanics are diverse and well developed, theft and murder being my favourites. Item RNG occasionally seems less helpful but guaranteed drops and well stocked shop keeps help alleviate that. If you take a diverse team items are plentiful and rarely useless but if you take a single type team you can tear though enemy defences at a breakneck pace. Only negative is the camera does not ignore the blocking wall closest to your camera resulting in you needing to use the tactical top-down camera that makes the game seem so less pretty.
Balance is fair and even but the elf nerfs before release makes them very unattractive for tactician or permadeath mode compared to all other races. Undead are amazing and used right get the min-maxer blood flowing.
Graphically the game is fantastic and beautiful and runs fine on my 1080, then again what doesn't. Spells and abilities are showy and well made, wish I could point out examples but they are all good.
Overall the game is fantastic and must have for any RPG or Tactical game lover who wants maximum bang for buck and to back a shining diamond in the pus-filled cesspit we call a games industry as well.

A labor of love, in search of greatness - 78/100
Owlboy is a neo-retro platforming adventure which aims to recapture the magic of the old 16-bit games we might have played back in the 90s. It was in development for nine years, and while it competes with the very best in some aspects, in others it falters, leaving a game which is good, but not great.
Pros:
- Beautiful pixel art, some of the best in any game, new or old
- Charming soundtrack
- Attention to detail in the animations, character/enemy design and other art
- Story holds attention, when it is being advanced
- Some good boss fights
- Collectables, upgrades, and secrets
- Heartwarming, non-cynical approach to dialogue and character design and development
Cons:
- Mediocre level design: 1. Lots of wasted space 2. Predictable, uninteresting layouts 3. Simplistic puzzles
- Combat feels perfunctory: 'shoot and they die', most enemies do not require any special tactics
- Controls are not 'tight' on the level of say, Shovel Knight or Ori and the Blind Forest
- Story advances slowly in the first 1/2 of the game, mostly predictable during this time
- World layout: 1. Sorely needs a map 2. Big, empty, and slow to traverse 3. Not always clear where you're supposed to go
- 'Saving the world' story is incongruous with the small handful friendly NPC's you encounter: no sense of the scope of conflict or story
Overall: A diamond in a fair amount of rough. Shovel Knight and Ori and the Blind Forest provide superior platforming experiences. Still fun and worth it however if you are a fan of the art and platformers in general.

Few months later I am looking for a game to play while searching Google for ARPG style games and this game was on the list.  Went back and re-looked at the game a second time.  The reviews are good, with what I would say is a 90% rating based on the number of positive to negative reviews.  Sometimes my gut is wrong, after reading recent reviews trolling the discussion I decided for the 30$ CAD it might be worth a look see.
There is a lot of goodness going on in this game; it pits you as the player against a dungeon master like character.  There is a randomness to the game that is fresh as you use decks of cards to determine how the game progresses.  This is an interesting concept, but there is a twist even through you can control the encounter deck, don’t expect the dealer to play fair especially as the game progresses.
The cards are dealt you move your table top piece unto the next encounter card, it plays out like a choose your own adventure novel, where you can encounter helpful goblins, or find yourself at the mercy of angry mobs.  There is also an arena type encounter where you fight in almost an arcade style fighting, cards determine how many mobs and of what type.  All leading to a Boss card at the end, the pace in the arcade game is pretty quick, but manageable even for old coots like myself.
IF anything, the game suffers a bit from a lack of a good tutorial, there is a small game to begin your series, but it lacks instructions, while it is not hard, it would be nice to understand the mechanics a bit more before you are thrown into the fray.  The arcade sequence is a bit twitch as you have to use wasd as movement, along with Q and the 1 and 2 buttons, as well as the spacebar.  I am more comfortable now, but there can be a lot going on when you are being attacked by a large group when you are trying to figure out the combat mechanics.
There is no game save feature, you play, leave and resume.  Not sure if you can start over even if you wanted too. It also offers no player avatar customization, so you can’t choose what your avatar looks like, pity I think that is important sometimes to create that affinity between the player and the game.
Overall 7.5/10, this is a good solid fun casual game that is unique to play.  It offers up a never ending play value as you never know what the cards will have in store for you.  I think a few tweaks and this game easily could be 10.  Buy it and support them in the Sequel HOF2.

Hard Reset is a laudable independent attempt at capturing the feel of classic-inspired "horde" first person shooters like Painkiller and Serious Sam. The early sensations are great, with a lush-looking Blade-Runner inspired aesthetic and a combat based on detonating strategically placed environmental hazards that will help you stop the hordes of robots running in your direction.
Unfortunately, that initial interest doesn´t last much longer. The gameplay turns up extremely shallow and repetitive by the third level, with the same hazards, enemies and pacing (get stuck in arena, kill all enemies, walk until next arena) over and over until the end of the game. The storytelling is dull, the extremely noisy and constrasty visuals full of flashing lights make almost impossible to realize what's happening on screen during the chaotic battles, so you just shoot randomly at moving things. There is barely anything during the game that will surprise you, so whereas the controls are comfortable and the game feels quite polished, the experience will be the exact same from the first to the last minute. "Hard Reset" is a clear example of a one-trick-pony of a game.
I'd recommend you to play the demo, but I wouldn't spend any money on the full game, since the game deflates almost since the beginning. A somewhat short game that will feel like takes too long to end out of the sheer repetition you'll feel along the journey.

Review:
Chivalry Mediavel Warfare is a very competitive, skill-based game with a medieval atmosphere. The combat are realistic and fast-paced. With 4 classes and over 60 weapons, you're almost sure to find a build that suits your fighting style. The game is based on skill and practice. You unlock weapon by using other weapons of the same category. The only things you can unlock with money is cosmetic, so it's not a Pay-To-Win. It has 5 interesting gamemodes and custom maps and mods.
Pro:
-Based on skill and practice. You can not pay to have upgrades you must practice to get better.
-Dragging, Matrixing and other such things are very fun to learn and use in fights, even if they bugs.
-Very fun, once you know how to fight.
-Lots of different builds possible.
-Team Objective, Team Deathmatch, Last Team Standing and Duel are fun and very easy to get better.
-Nice graphics.
Con:
-Lots of hackers and team-killers on beginner servers- unintentional for the latter. And when you accuse someone of hacking, other people say you're a newbie and you don't know the game.
-Lots of intentional team-killers on normal servers.
-There is a huge difference of skills between beginner servers and normal servers.
-The community can be very toxic with its hackers, team-killers, ragers and other such people.
-If you've got a high ping or more than 10-15% team damage, you're gonna get kick.
-It's very long and hard to be good. It took me 10 hours to be half-way decent on beginner servers. It takes hundred of hours to be good on normal server. And all the while you're gonna get destroy by better people and end the game with 2/23/4.
-The devs have stopped working on the games. That means all the little annoying bugs aren't going to get fixed. On the other side, positive bugs suchs as dragging aren't gonna get removed either.
Beginner tips:
-First thing you should do after buying the game is the Training Map. Go in Training then Training Map. It shows you have to block, attack, combo, feint and how to play the different classes. It's very useful at the beginning.
-Use a shield. Don't hold it in position all the time but use it to block more easily until you get used to the speed of the weapons and dragging.
-If you're playing as a Vanguard or a Knight, don't side-swing in team games. You're gonna end up killing more allies than ennemies and get kick.
-If you like to do a lot of burst damage and have a good defense, pick Knight. If you like to do a lot of damage and keep your distance use Vanguard. If you like to attack very fast use Man-At-Arm.
-Don't play Archer until you're used to blocking with a sword. Archer is the hardest class to master.
-Stick to beginner servers until you're level 10 to 15. But don't wait until you're 16 to play on normal server or it'll be twice as hard.

First came out a while back and became my favorite game of all times.
Then the game slowly started to give credits and encourage the use of glitches and completely unrealistic behavior, to the point of giving tips on how to use them and giving birth to what is without a doubt one of the worst community I've ever seen on steam.
Feinting was the first step to the fall of Chivalry. Because, sorry to break it to you guys, you can't just start swinging a 5kg flamberge and just straight up stop in mid-air to swing again in the next second. That's not how physics work.
Speaking of physics, dragging. If you thought feinting wasn't realistic, wait to see a fully-armored knight just ballet-dancing with a 10kg maul. That's to give you and idea how bad this is.
The idea of dragging is to delay the strike's landing through ballet-dancing. I'm not kidding, that's all it really looks like. And so, back to physics : That could indeed work if you still had some attack-speed in the actual landing of the weapon. Because, yet again, sorry to break it to you, but just touching someone with the tip of the sharpest blade wont hurt him at all. It might actually tickle in a very pleasant way, but that's all you're gonna get.
And so I thank you, makers of this fine game, for turning the dream of medieval warfare and my formerly favorite game into this nonsensical piece of garbage. I'm sure you've pleased a lot of call of duty fanboys out there.
You may take the obvious frustration with which I wrote this review as my final opinion on it. Chivalry : Medieval Warfare is litteraly painfully frustrating to play, and I wouldn't recommend it to anyone. It's addictive and will turn you into an angry beast. Spare your wallet and your blood pressure : DO NOT, EVER, BUY THIS GAME.
Arby out.

I can tell you one thing about this game, it's so time consuming you won't even realize the time is gone.
But that's one of the problems though, is that the game can literally go on for 7 hours.
It takes about 40 mins to build one of the Tier 3 things, and you either make like 50 engineers to work on it, or you wait an hour to get something built.
The combat however, is fun. You can make a crap load of troops and just have a massive battle. It feels like a real war, and it isn't like AoE where you can only have about 200 troops total.
Unit diversity is key here. Unlike AoE 3, you cannot win by having a massive spam of the same few units.
( AoE 3: 50 Skirmishers, 50 Uhlans, 20 Falconets and the rest musketeers )
This does make early combat VERY boring though, as several base turrets will mow down hundreds of your troops, which take about 7 seconds each.
There's LAND, AIR, and NAVAL combat, all in one. ( Some maps don't have water )
The actual involvement in combat is very little though, there isn't much to do, formations don't really matter, and it's hard to get a proper battle formation, because of the way the formations work. There aren't any abilities or anything either, and you can't really do much micro-ing, because everyone can just turn around and shoot while running, so there isn't really any point. Units die extremely quick anyways, so having a small army is meaningless unless they're high tier.
The 3 factions in the game don't really add any diversity whatsoever.
I think it's to balance the game, but it kinda makes it dull. The only difference is the way the look.
The game is buggy on every OS that isn't Windows XP, so make sure you use a service pack or something.
There's a LOT of building required in this game. You have to probably build bases that are 1/10th of the map (By the Tier 3) I feel like there's too much focused on construction. I think I'm just building stuff 80% of the time.
I can't find anyone to play multiplayer with, but when I look at it there were some pretty cool things. You can switch sides, and ally with people and stuff, just like AoE 2. You can also share resources if needed.
Overall, I think it's a worth while game, but only for people who really want to play strategy, otherwise, it can be hard to get into.

The Metro series are some of my favorite First Person shooters of all time, and i'll try to explain why I love Metro Last Light so much with Pro's and Con's.
Pro's:
+One of the greatest atmosphere's in any of the games i've played, it has kind've a survival horror atmosphere to it, with tight tunnels, dark corridors, and crumbling buildings. And  when you finally go into the outside world, its frightening, enemies usually attack when your least expecting it, and  slowly trudging through the deep snow.....knowing your alone.
+Gameplay is fun and has much to offer, there is many guns, explosives, and attachments for your guns. Keep in mind Metro isnt a Run'n'gun fast paced shooter like Doom or Quake, metro doesnt throw tons of enemies at you, enemy encounters are dangerous, especially with monsters, knowing that you have to be careful, and that your not some super powerful super soldier, but a young man fighting to survive the cold and brutal apocolypse.
+Graphics are very good, there is some amazing lighting effects here, and going through tunnels and towns in the sewers looks great.
+A very intriguing story, that continues off Metro 2033 beautifully, it continues the story of Artyom, and has an extremely good plot and writing.
+Characters and their voice acting is superb, at least in my opinion.
Now for only one con i have with the game.
-I ran into a few screen freezes, and while there wasnt a ton of them, it was pretty annoying, I by no means have a potato pc, i have a I7 7700k, and a 1070 ti, so its not like im running it below the requirements.
Despite a few freezes here and there, Metro Last Light is an amazing, atmospheric FPS that I wholeheartedly recommend to anyone.

I received this game gifted from a friend, and I've had a lot of fun with it!  Current progress is ~50%.  Yes, it's a bit tedious for most people and yes... it's essentially a clone of Battleship.  With slightly more turn-based strategy as you progress.  I think the AI is just right for this game (not incredibly smart / cheating), so that makes it a bit easier to win.
Mutliple reviewers are saying the enemy's location is up to a complete guess.  When I first started playing I also believed this to be true.  However, this is not true once you learn more of the gameplay and proceed further into the missions.  Here are some tips for those struggling (because I didn't realize these are first either):
1. The enemy's long artillery are only oriented in one direction (facing you).  So don't be trying to find pieces oriented in the other direction.
2. Pay attention to indicators on the ground if you miss a shot.  If there was a red radar-like indicator, it means the enemy has a unit on a nearby square.  This can be likened to Minesweeper.
3. You earn money faster as you progress through the missions (the bonus missions help too), so it's not as bleak as when you first start out.
4. Use your weapon upgrades wisely.  IMO better to have more weapon abilities & shots per turn than pieces on your board.
To conclude, I think this is a fine turn-based war game for the $4 price tag.  But I completely understand how it would be boring for most people.

No, I don't recommend it. The game is simple enough to pick up, just press "Go". All you need to do is setup an army, evolve and fuse them, place them in a formation on a 3x5 grid, then press "Go" the whole way.  Archers in the back, melee in the front. This game is meant for the mobile community with the incessant pleading to buy beginner's packs. There is a very strong Pay To Win Mechanism, refer to CONS for more details. It's like one of your Facebook games, don't forget to add your friends. It's not supposed to be on Steam.
1. 8 Chapters
They put in the effort to make 8 stages.
2. Simple to Learn
Just press "Go"
3. Collecting Sets of Creatures
Easy enough to do. These things come automatically as you progress in the game.
4. Artwork
All the monsters look good even though there is repetitive artwork. E.g. Wolf, big Wolf, bigger Wolf. Blue Frog, Red Frog, Black Frog.
5. Castle
The castle is pretty good, you get to build stuff, though it's like Farmville upgrading. You need to farm Wood, Stone and Magic Orbs to upgrade every single building in the Castle.
1. Repetitive and Boring Mechanic
The game isn't just Press Go as you can move units around mid battle, heal, cast spells, items and add more summons. However, casting spells, reviving and items require cash shop items that totally ruin the experience. E.g. Thor's Hammer Deal 900 damage to all enemies, is a cash shop item.
2. Paywall
You need to pay to get more meat for more energy to play the game. There's a $2.99 Beginner's Pack for a Tier 5 Elite Dragon and a Tier 4 Elite Lion, 500,000 gold, 250 gems, 5 Thor Hammers and 5 Ruby Stones. This just sets  a precedent for more Pay-To-Win
3. Not All Creatures Can Evolve
Some creatures like the slug can't evolve.
4. Pay To Win List
a. $99.99 for 7500 gems
b. VIP Powers. VIP Level 25. Buy 2,500,000 Gems (They call it Eternal Overlord)
+25% Gems for Bank Purchases
+500,000,000 Gold
+1200 Food and 170 Chili
+2000 Time Turners
+15 Golden Keys
5. Time Turners
Used for Auto Mode on stages. They actually sell you things for automating pressing "Go". 4 Gems for 1 Time Turner.
6. Fast Forward Button
There isn't a need to play the game. Just press Fast Forward and it's all over.
7. You need to be Rank 5 for Multiplayer Combat
Everything from Rank 1 to 4 is just tutorial.

Hand of Fate is a card game developed and published by Defiant Development. As mentioned previously, Hand of Fate is a card game brought to life with Batman Arkham style combat and deckbuilding to customize your events and equipment pool. It also offers an endless mode where you have to survive for as long as possible with every card you've ever gotten mixed in the frey
The game offers responsive combat and a huge variety of equipment, monsters and events. The card artwork on each card given to you is really well made and fantastic music by Jeff van Dyck
The dealers narration is well-produced. There is a fairly lengthy story mode and a more rogue-like endless mode and the game offers a very stylized graphics that looks great. The game dynamically get's more difficult as your opponent's own deck improves alongside yours with more enemies and negative outcomes the more you progress
However, bosses are fairly week when you first encounter them so it feels sligthly anti-climactic and several of the weapons are straight up just upgrades over others meaning that meta decks get very similar. Every weapon is one handed so despite what you're using combat is always the same mostly, also the animations during combat are pretty weak
I really did enjoy Hand of Fate, I highly recommend this game for anyone looking for a good rogue-like and also for people unfamiliar with the genre and want a more simplistic game with easy to learn but hard to master combat and with all the little issues the game has, I hope these will be ironed out in Hand of Fate 2!

"Oh god why" is the only way I can start this. Damn. This game has a story, and while it is basically more of an interactive movie, it is a really thrilling one. The story is all the force this game has - but only that, sadly.
Yes, it is damn enjoyable to uncover what has happened to the protagonist and his surroundings. Don't get me wrong, I'm all up for discovering secrets and clearing up ties between clues in a murder case. But it isn't like this. Most of the clues are just randomly placed in the world with no visible or logical correlation, forcing you to just waste your time on fiding them. And then there's the random demon, which, after destroying one of them, are barely a challenge, and mostly just an annoyance that you have to clear when you travel to the next level.
And thats just sad, because the story is good, the audio is good, the graphics are well enough for a 2014 game and it runs butter-smooth - no "cinematic 24 fps", no stutter and no input lag.
