My scores:
world: 9/10
main story arc: 8/10
characters: 7/10
role-playing elements: 5/10
side missions: 2/10 (don't even bother)
loyalty missions: 6/10
presentation: 8/10
combat: 6/10
Detailed opinion:
I've heard a lot about that game, but I'm kinda disappointed. I'm fan of sci-fi genre, and was expecting a lot (Mass Effect 2 is the first game I played). At the end, the feelings are mixed. The story is very good, and the world is detailed and interesting. Characters are a mixed bag, some of the characters are very well written (Mordin, Grunt, Tali, Morinth), some are just dull (Miranda and Jacob). The protagonist itself is also somewhat one-dimensional and doesn't make a lot of sense. For example if you play paragon, you are good all-loving paladin, but has no problem whatsoever killing hundreds of minions during the mission.
The main issue I had with the game, is it's mechanics. It is simply not good enough. You would expect some choices to make from an acclaimed RPG title, but all you can do - is plow though hundreds of dull enemies in a linear corridor-like missions. Many missions start with a good premises (i.e. politics, character development, etc) but no, every goddamn single time it ends up with the same boring killing of hordes of enemies. And the combat isn't even that fun. I never had console and admittedly not very familiar with thirds-person shooter genre, but I do enjoy good fighting. Here the fighting in the game felt really boring and dull. Every time I had a fighting part, I was just thinking to myself "not again" and wanted to get over with it as quickly as possible. Also I didn't see any real difference with taking different companions - they all performed more or less the same, with no synergy or strategy whatsoever involved in choosing them (even if it made difference you don't even know what the mission will be, so you can't make an informed choice).
Another complain I had - is that loyalty missions were very much similar, almost all of them involved some kind disappointment with close relative and again tons of goddamn fighting which often didn't fit thematically. Few were nice exceptions (notably Legion and Jack) but the majority were quite boring. Side missions on other side were complete and utter waste of time. I usually do like to go through all side missions in RPG games I play, but here I stopped doing any side quests completely after a while as they were lacking and real substance or fun.
Anyway, I finished the game and somewhat enjoyed it, but I'm not sure I would recommend the game of play it ever again myself.

Ищем причину потратить 104  рублей по скидке и 419 рублей без скидки, на немного улучшенную дилогию Metro. Частично удается: Metro 2033 Redux стала намного лучше, а вот смысл в покупке Last Light Redux найдут лишь самые заядлые фанаты.
Дмитрий Глуховский написал не шибко интересный роман «Метро 2033» и однажды проснулся знаменитым. Выкладывая в интернет главы и попутно обивая пороги издательств, в один день начинающему писателю и опытному журналисту улыбнулась удача: книгу взялись выпустить на бумаге. С тех пор (2005 год) вышло продолжение «Метро 2034» и скоро ожидается релиз «Метро 2035». Сеттинг франшизы отлично подходит под игровую адаптацию, поэтому появление шутера не заставило себя долго ждать. Обе части, Metro 2033 и Metro: Last Light, хорошо встречены общественностью.
2 игры получили улучшения и доработки, однако реально заметно это лишь в первой — Metro 2033. Потому как в Last Light Redux изменений кот наплакал: «по просьбам фанатов», как говорят сами разработчики, в игру добавили невероятно важную опцию — посмотреть на часы и заглянуть в инвентарь. Чувствуете глубину изменений, за которые просят $15 (или 7$, если уже куплена Last Light)? Ах да, еще тут есть улучшенная анимация ближнего боя и тихих убийств. Этого все равно преступно мало для того, чтобы вновь просить деньги за игру. Такие изменения можно и в патче сделать, на худой конец — в DLC за 1-2 доллара.
Зато с Metro 2033 Redux ситуация совсем другая. Игра вышла в 2010 году и на тот момент выглядела очень недурно: передовые технологии, четкие текстуры, хорошая работа с освещением и при этом относительно неплохая оптимизация. Но время идет, и сейчас шутер четырехлетней давности выглядит не столь впечатляюще. Поэтому 4AGames перенесла Metro 2033 на последнюю версию движка 4AEngine. Результат заметен невооруженным взглядом. Совершенно иного уровня освещение, эффекты в разы красивее, объемный туман и дым, которые хочется развеять рукой. При этом игра избавилась от большинства болячек, вроде беспричинных просадок кадров в секунду, графических багов и других огорчающих моментов из оригинальной версии. Только вот трупы по-прежнему могут проваливаться сквозь объекты: то нога монстра будет торчать из бетонной плиты, то полтуловища уйдет в стену. Также никуда не делись бесконечные орды противников — будут переть, пока не выполните задание. К счастью, таких эпизодов мало на протяжении шести-семичасовой кампании.
Которая все так же интересна, и парочку изменений в Last Light сугубо для фанатов. Приобретать обе части есть смысл, только если до этого не играли в Last Light. Но игры вышли топово!!!!

This game is one-of-a-kind. Although I have spent tens of hours playing it, I have yet to beat it.
The point of the game is to advance throughout a deck of cards, moving a token on the card and revealing challanges or events along the way. As you build your deck with better equipment and event cards, you have a higher penalty for higher rewards, making the game swing either way depending on how you improve while you play.
The combat system is simple and works as a junior version of the batman combat system. It isn't really where the game shines, though it offers many difficulties on its own when multiple enemy types are fought in one combat session.
The graphics for the dealer and cards are nice, but the combat graphics look plastered on. If you're anal retentive about everything in your game being beatufiul, move on.
My overall point is this: If you like collecting things, you'll love this game. You have to replay scenarios over and over unless you're skilled at following the cards, and when you finally get the beast gear from all the tokens in the game you can beat it relatively easily. But if you don't like attempting the same checks over and over and don't want to spend higher than 10 hours into a game like this, you probably won't beat it as I find the best tokens in the game are extremely hard to obtain.

This game is amazing in almost every aspect. The music, aesthetics, gameplay, soundeffects, characters and so forth.
Everything is neatly tied together and has formed this amazing experience called Owlboy. Even if the game felt a bit short, I can't help but feel satisfied with the game in the end. Owlboy was a huge enjoyment for me, the controls were tight and felt amazing to play around with and the level design completmented the overall gameplay very well. Furthermore, the music and art for this game was jawdropping, it added so much character to the game and so much charm and (to me atleast) the artstyle feels unique and stands out from other pixelart games, as this feels like a mix between old and new. Thus all locations and characters are memorable and loveable. Not only does the game offer something pleasant to look at, but the story was quite good as well. Owlboy had interesting characters with nice and somewhat unexpected twists, although nothing to write home about. To fully understand what I am talking about one has to experience Owlboy themselves.
The only thing I can see people complain about is that the game can be a bit pricey. 22,99€ is quite a lot of money for a ~6 hour long game, however Owlboy brings an innovative prespective of the platforming genre and the whole experience is truly magnificent. When I finished the game, I thought to myself "Well, this was a bit short. Was it really worth all the money?". At the same moment I asked myself that I noticed how dumb that question was, as I already know the answer.
Yes, it was worth every penny. If you think you might enjoy this game, I'd suggest you purchase it right away as it is one of the most unique Indie experiences I've had in a long time.
Pros:
+ Art and Music = Jawdropping
+ Gameplay felt good, smooth and natural
+ Good level design
+ Likeable characters
Cons:
- Can be a tad bit pricey
Hope you found my thoughts helpful even though I didn't cover every aspect of the game!

A surprisingly fun game.
By over 80% of the playtime you basically play a single player 3D clone of "Talisman" with a charismatic Dealer who serves maybe not as your opponent but more like a narrator or generally speaking - a game master.  He is responsible for creating a randomly shaped path builded with  covered random cards for your advancing pawn. Each move of the represenation of your hero means one random event happening to you. Mostly it's just an adventure text quest with A,B,C-type decisions based on luck or wise choice. However sometimes "stepping on" the card triggers a combat sequence against multiple aggressors.
In this phase the game changes drastically because now you are not only reading the text and wishing for a good karma but actively participate in a visalisation of the event by controling your "pawn hero" in hack&slash minigame environment with a very fluid and enjoyable fighting system based on freeflow mechanics (known from Assassins Creed or Batman:Asylum series).
Taking the "matters into yours own hands" is a nice gateway because only reading the text and listening to the Dealer could make you drowsy after a longer session. You can choose the difficulty of these fights however take in mind that combat can get really challenging and perhaps even frustrating on Hard mode.
If I could choose major drawbacks of this title ... well:
you can't customize a physical appearance of the hero. You always play as a bearded and mohawk hair-styled warrior who doesn't look differently than other human mobs you are fighting with. This kinda sucks but at least all equippable items like armors or helmets are visible on character so it helps to set your hero apart from other human enemies.
And the flaw connected with the combat:
Framerate sometimes get choppy when you fight with more than dozen opponents but that's a "beauty" of used Unity engine.
So to sum up it's an innovative, enjoyable and balanced mix of board game with a real-time action sequences. It's worth trying expecially if you are "Talisman: The Magical Quest" game fan.

When i first heard about Hand of Fate, i was immediatly intrigued. An RPG with deckbuilding that allows me to play out Encounters in action-combat rather than stats and turn based strategy? Certainly an interesting twist on the Genre.
When i finally got to play it, it delivered on almost everything i had hoped for. There is deep strategy at play when you carefully pick what equipment and what encounters to mix into your upcoming adventure (even though the recommended decks are fully sufficient for players that aren't interested in min-maxing) and though there are chance based encounters the game gives you an edge by letting you pick from an array of 4 Success- and Failure Cards (revealed then shuffled) in a way similar to popular shell games infamous for street trickery. If you're quick on the eyes, or lucky, you might be able to cheat the odds a bit in your favor.
So how does the game actually work? You move your hero across playing fields made up out of cards, with each card presenting you a different encounter. Some are simply combat or shops, others have choices for you to make, stories to progress, or gambles to take. But depending on the main villain you are seeking to defeat on your run, the dealer may mix his own set of encounters and cards into the deck with yours, so you can sometimes run into unexpected challenges. Moving consumes food, which heals health lost in combat, but also forces you to invest into getting more food, or starvation will start to take away your health. And losing to Starvation is a really boring way to die. So you can be tempted to mix extra combat encounters into the deck, just to have a reliable source of gain cards from killed opponents, but the more times you fight, the higher the chance the dealer will draw something nasty from the enemies deck that also eventually contains all the bosses you've defeat on previous runs.
When combat itself is due, the game changes into a 3D Action Combat in the style of the Batman Games. It's fought in various sizes and shapes of arenas, from molten volcano craters to eerie forest paths and river bridges. Taking a good look around during the spawning animation into the environment can give you an edge on your opponents, as traps are spread out everywhere and can be triggered by both you and your enemies. There's few more satisfying things than seeing a pesky ratman step on a spiketrap or to see a skeleton shattered by an arrow trap. The combat is a bit on the simplistic side and it is where the Unity Engine meets its limits on the graphical side of things, but while enemies may not look like they're made with lifelike detail, the very distinct artstyle still fits very well overall and creates a believable fantasy world.
If there's any gripes i have with the game, it's that i can't customize my own hero visually beyond what equipment i stick on him and that SOME of the cards you can draw especially later in the game when enemies start a tendency to curse you can be a bit overwhelming on the resource side of things. I ran into a curse named Midas's Hunger that converted all my food into Gold 1:1 and made me eat 10 gold with each step, so that i started starving to death pretty much immediatly after. BUT overall the game does seem very well balanced.
I think Hand of Fate is worth your time just for the unique experience it offers. The combat may play out a bit simply and at times outright easy once you've learned how to utilize blocking and countering, but it's still fun and actually rewarding to do well or even perfect in combat as it helps you boost your run with additionally gained resources. And, as one of the games biggest strengths, no run is ever truely "Lost", despite the permadeath system. Each new encounter card you complete will reward you with its "Token" at the end of the run, which will crack open in a satisfying animation and give you more gear and more encounters with their own tokens to create stories and rewards that unfolds across multiple runs. There is never true failure, as you'll always manage to make SOME progression, even if you don't take down one of the main villains of the game.
On top of it all, there's endless mode, where you can keep exploring and fighting forever to rack up an ever increasing score, and if you're good in combat you can set records to compare and brag to your friends. Unfortunately the game doesn't have multiplayer, but it doesn't really need one. It's an intense experience on its own, and even has a bunch of free already included DLC story- (and thus card) lines added for you to unlock as you make your way through your adventures.
Overall, i'd say Hand of Fate is almost a must buy for anyone who likes RPGs and Action Combat Systems. And i have to give huge credit to the voice actor for the card dealer, he does a job as impressive and immersing as almost no other in all the games i've played.

Not so much a game as a scenario generator set in feudal era Europe.  The point of the game is to keep your family legacy alive, with anything else you achieve in the meantime bolstering your end game score.  How you choose to grow that legacy depends upon your ambition, the intentions of those around you, and a bit of luck.  Everything in this game is obscure, and attempting to play without first digging through the chuncky tutorials will leave most people hopelessly lost.  Even with the tutorial and a firm sense of how you intend to grow your legacy, a lot of gameplay revolves around watching the timer tick away and waiting for something interesting to happen.  This game will create some interesting stories to tell your friends (Like how you wound up King of a major empire because you NPC father embarked on a conquest campaign, or how you yourself worked to grow a united kingdom, only to watch it torn apart by your ungrateful children after your first character's death).  Fans of idle games and history buffs will probably get a thrill out of this title, but people looking for a more conventional gaming experience should probably look elsewhere.

One of the biggest Steam purchase disappointments I ever had. Not that watching the trailer didn't provide its share of warning signs. But I didn't listen to my gut feeling. First of all, the engine turned out to be to be much more crude and basic than I expected, and the puzzles (at least in the first 2 cases) provided zero challenge value. The art design, music and the graphics are, however, excellent, and probably the main reason people choose to ignore the game's staggering flaws.
What could offset the pedestrian gameplay is the story and characters, of course, but the game falls terribly flat here, providing a pre-teen level of storytelling and characterisation, not to mention the insufferable forcing of continuously uninspired humour, whose painful delivery is placed completely above any attempt to provide a compelling story and characters. It's like an extreme case of Sword & Sworcery, where a brilliantly looking game with a wonderfully atmosphere and art design is in such a jarring opposition to the quality of its story and writing, it's tragic to witness it.
I don't have a habit of writing reviews here, but this is by far the most deceiving ratio of approval in comparison with the product quality I ever experience on this platform, so I felt a need to compile a personal disapproval. Hopefully my review will make some people think twice before buying this without trying the demo.
It is definitely worrying to see this amount of praise and approval, Steam curators included (!), for such a dubious product. I expected for the Indie game audience to have more sense.
I'm on the verge for asking a refund, but I will probably keep the game as a reminder of my folly, to consider a purchase more critically...next time I see pretty graphics.

Valkyria Chronicles is an interesting mix of genres. The combining of third person shooting and turn based strategy seems awkward on paper, but works out quite well in practice. That combined with the unique and beautiful art style and the surprisingly interesting story makes Valkyria Chronicles a game that deserves your attention.
On the surface the mechanics of Valkyria Chronicles seem pretty straight forward, if unique. Select a unit, move the unit, perform an action and repeat until you are out of actions. In reality it is made much more complex by the unit types, need for cover, and the fact that you can select the same unit more than once per turn. These simple aspects change the engagements in surprising ways.
After selecting a unit the player must move the unit into position with movement being limited by a meter that depletes as the unit moves. Once in position the player takes aim manually and attacks or performs an action or simply ends turn. This repeats until the command point available are used up or the player ends their turn. The enemy turn plays out then the player takes their next turn.
There are five types of troop the player can command. Scouts can run far and use a rifle in combat, snipers are what you would expect, lancers are your rocket launcher types, shock troopers use machine guns, and engineers are able to build or remove obstacles and mines and can repair tanks. There is also a tank, sometimes two, that have a variety of weapons and require two command points to use. All of the troops available have unique personalities and strengths and weaknesses. They also all relate to one another in different ways, with some being fond of each other and gaining bonuses when together.
The story is a story of war, love, and loss with some supernatural elements. It touches on some fairly mature themes, such as racism, and handles them with a level of respect not always seen in games. As a whole the story is an allegory for the second world war with highly fictionalized elements.
The art style, dubbed the canvas engine, is a unique and beautiful anime style that looks like a moving painting. The models are largely lacking detail but the design and canvas engine make up for it.
Valkyria Chronicles is a must play for strategy fans. The unique game play and art styles combined with a genuinely interesting and moving story makes it an instant classic.

The biggest issue NeuroVoider faces is that its level of randomization and customization is nowhere near what the game's trailer suggests.
You get to select a player class, which really only alters your special move (a dash, a shield, or a sort of berzerker mode); you can select second special of your choosing, an active or passive ability of your choice; you can select your two weapons, and while there are a staggering amount of different options, you'll soon find two that work best for you and seldom even look at other variations; and you can select your head, body, and locomotion modules, but each of them are basically flatly 'upgrades' or 'downgrades' with very minor differences between base stats to act as sidegrades.
Similarly, most enemies are very similar: Swarms of minor enemies, the occasional big, tough enemy, and four main bosses that are effectively all the same boss with minor weapon variants. As a result, the same strategy you use on any given stage should work pretty well on all of them. Also, most of the stages are very similar - there aren't really any interesting rooms or setpieces like most roguelites and most of the different location options look, honestly, visually very similar as well. I makes the option of location feel kind of pointless, really, aside from the differences in loot amount elite enemies, and general map size.
The end result is a game that lures you in with the promise of tons of customization, but you spend far more of your time just grinding and upgrading your setup that works for you to help you take down slightly stronger variations of the same enemies again and again than you do customizing anything or trying to tailor your approach to specific obsticles. And, of course, since 90% of your customization is straight upgrades, you really don't even feel that sense of lucky/unlucky a loot-based roguelite should give by dropping particularly grand loot in your lap or lackthereof - you'll get it eventually because it's just part of the game's progression.
Might recommend to specific people on sale, would not recommend at full price.

What to say about Recettear: An item shop's Tale.
If I would have to choose a single word to describe this game it would be “silly” to which that isn’t a bad thing. I find myself coming back to this game every now and again just for its simple game mechanics. Be it in the shop selling off my items or crawling through some dungeon hoping to score some high priced loot for cheap.
Though I do find some of the name of the characters a little annoying but that is a minor quip at best. There is a story too this game, though I haven’t dived too deep into it if there is anything past paying off the initial debt.
The dungeon crawling is pretty simple though with a slight twist. The protagonist and her fairy partner follow behind a ‘hero’ who you will be in control of. The idea is you get a box that can hold only so many items that includes whatever healing item you think you might need or if you just want to improve the gear the hero is wearing but has yet to buy the upgrades from you. This will cut down on room for potential loot since you will be holding onto their equipment to give back to them after you leave the dungeon. Though if the hero falls you can only store 1 of these items in a box as you take the injured hero and get the hell out of there.
There are several heroes to be had. The first is a standard fighter. As the game moves forward you will meet different heroes who play differently from one another and have their own amusing personality and kind of annoying names as I stated above
You can customize the stores atmosphere by changing up the counters, walls and floors which can change it to Gaudy or plain store as well as a light or dark theme which will affect how you attract customers.
So all in all it is an easy game to jump into and jump out of which is why I enjoy it so much you can leave it for days even years then all of a sudden jump right back in and spend countless hours making as much money as you want.

Murdered: Soul Suspect - an AAA 21th century quest title. Or adventure, if you like that definition more. Main mission of the whole game is to fugure out how to move to the next level, optionally helping some other people on the way.
1. Gameplay. That's the game where you will not be shooting, or fighting. Except of dodging and expelling some hollow wraiths from time to time, by stalking them from behind and clicking a button to win. On the top of things, you'll be searching for pieces of evidence, and making some investigation going through and through some unpleasant secrets, revolving mostly around old dark history of the town you're settled in.
Other than that, you can roam the levels in search of collectables, using your ghost powers to unlock all the achievements and background spooky stories which that game holding under the counter.
2. Troubles. Game is buggy. Not messy or totally out of control, but I had to reload the starting sequence two times, unable to "follow the light", and later there was a museum bug (right after the running train part). Those two mentioned  bugs aren't really game breaking, but quite severe, the way I see things. Especially the first one: sure, it's just the start of the game, but, intro video is unskippable, duh!
Other than those bugs (and some smaller), and the point that not everyone might like a point-n-click adventure with oversized "search for scrappy notes" part and "open-world roaming" like in the Batman games, where not all places are opened from the start... I am out with any other reasons why you may not like the game.
3. Summary. Sure, the visuals aren't really top-notch, and the story is maybe too short for such a project... the actions gets repetative after a little while, and all that "hiding from wraiths" part is not too pleasant... but hey! - every, EVERY game has some weak spots, and someone will not be pleased with it.
But, from my point of view, it's really a great game. A piece where you don't need to stab, kick or blast your way through is always a rarety. Ability to help some bystanders while doing you main quest, by putting some of you abilities in a good use, is surely a nice addition to the game's pro sides. Finally, a well-written detective story is always a welcome on my bookshelf. So, I'll mark Murdered: Soul Suspect with 8/10. Not perfect, but really good game which I'm glad I've played.

I've been trying to make this game work as a local multiplayer couch game with a friend for a couple weeks now, and we just can't do it. It's got lots of appeal - the awesome sprite art, good soundtrack, fun upgrade system - but we'd feel pissy and ripped off after every game session.
The difficulty is just so uneven. Hordes and hordes of inconsequential enemies that do no damage, even whole stages where you don't get hit at all, and then all of a sudden you get instagibbed for half or all your health by an enemy that's not even on screen. It's a natural byproduct of the procedurally generated weapons but it makes the game feel like a crapshoot. We'd spend a good hour on a run without any challenge and then get annihilated by a boss or elite before we even knew what was going on.
It's not exactly that mechanically precise, either, especially if you're playing with a controller, so the difficulty isn't something you can work around. Everything's just sort of a chaotic mess and it's hard to tell which attacks are the meaningless grunt ones, and which are the instagibs.
I dunno, maybe it's better as a single player experience but as a multiplayer game this is definitely a pass. If you're looking for another counterpart to crawl/nidhogg/broforce etc like I was, this is not it.

It would be an understatement to say that the roguelike market is oversaturated; it seems like it gets harder every day to find a roguelike that is forging new ground in terms of gameplay or mechanics.  In that sense, NeuroVoider is a breath of fresh air.  The weapons are fun, mechanically diverse, satisfying to use, and punchy.  The hook of upgrading your own body with the parts of your enemies feels extremely rewarding and keeps gameplay fresh no matter how far you go.  The bosses and enemies are difficult, but never feel unfair; I've never felt cheated when I died, as it was always due to a series of mistakes during gameplay, or because I didn't allocate resources correctly to keep up with the difficulty curve.
I would put this game on the same tier as Nuclear Throne or Enter the Gungeon.  It is a shining example of how to do a roguelite correctly, and the best thing that could happen for the genre would be for developers to shamelessly steal from this game when they're developing their own game mechanically.  On top of all of that, it also has a fun setting, a great co-op mode, and the pixel art is top notch.  Frankly, I'm shocked this game hasn't gotten more time on the steam front page, and I'm disappointed that I needed to find this myself instead of Steam simply serving it to me when I'm looking for new games to play.
It's probably a good sign if my only complaint is "I wish I'd known about it sooner." Check it out.

Now, if you ask the general public, they will most likely say that it is ETS2-remake, with a new price tag. Some will also say that it's just DLC... I highly disagree

This game has a very small selection of trucks. And yes, that is quite annoying currently, but there is more to come. With the 3 trucks currently available, there's still a lot of customization, and new opportunities. I can't wait to see what new trucks they'll be bringing out.

to
. But that's perfectly fine. In this game, you'll see the deserts, you'll see the winding roads, the large highways. And as you change from state to state, you'll see differences in speed limits, which drastically change your driving
This brings me onto the map. Currently, the map, as small as it is, is still pretty damn large. Just the state of California is about the same size as the UK from ETS2. The map is large right now, and can only get bigger, and I am excited to see what is coming soon!
Should you buy this game? Well, if you like realistic driving, and beautiful scenery, Yeah. If you're looking for a casual driver, yeah. If you're looking for a reckless driving thing that resembles Grand Theft Auto, no. This game is perfect for the trucker-in-training!

I have to say that I am quite impressed with this game, having played almost every truck sim in the 18 WoS days as well as ETS2. I remember many years ago, stumbling acorss
to find that the domain was being held for future use, I had high hopes for the game when it was finally released, and SCS didn't disappoint.
Initially, my biggest concern was that the environment and feel was going to be too much like what Europe thinks of North America rather than what it's really like over here, and while it's difficult to explain, those elements do exist, but fortunately not to the degree I had initially thought. Screenshots of the game in the past year kind of made me worry about this, but the initial release isn't so bad.
My favourite thing is that they've solved pretty much every issue I had in terms of driving physics - problems that were present in past games and even ETS2. With the transmission setting set to advanced, the game allows for clutchless shifting (with proper timing, naturally) with controllers like the G27, and the engine doesn't have the torque converter feel where applying throttle doesn't instantly raise the rpm by a couple hundred. If you're not sure what I mean, play ETS2 with a high horsepower truck like an FH with 750hp and while coasting, hit the gas and watch the tach.
One of the things I wasn't fond of in ETS2 is the fact that many cities and roads are so hard to differentiate. I could never find my way around if not for the GPS. The Scandinavia DLC is an exception to this IMO, but it seems like every city and highway is mostly the same. ATS on the other hand, has very original and unique areas, as well as cities of varying sizes. I hope that this, plus the fact that they'll be releasing the map in bits at a time, will mean that we can sort of learn our way around through experience, and certain areas and roads will become more familiar overtime. I'm really glad to see SCS try to make each area of the map unique, original, and realistic.
A number of people have complained about the current lack of trucks, many saying that they should have done like they did with ETS2 and release them unlicensed first. I think that there is a lot of legal mumbo jumbo involved. It's hard to criticize SCS for this when you don't know what their legal obligations are, and where they are currently at with truck manufacturers.
There's still things I'd like to see improved, like the audio, but I can't even imagine how hard it is to make a realistic sounding truck without hearing audio loops and allowing it to fluently change as engine rpm increases and decreases, or even as more or less throttle is applied. With each truck so far, as engine rpm increases it seems to go through 'waves' for lack of a better word, where once you hit 12 or 1300 rpm, the tone resets down to sound lower again. Again, difficult to explain.
Kudos to SCS Software. They're definitely on the right track. My favourite thing about them as a developer is that they listen to their community very actively and are quick to make changes if needed. This game was released at a lower than expected price point and I am very, very eager to see where ATS goes in the future.
I highly recommend this game to anyone looking for a relaxing but enjoyable simulator, not only for the game but for the amazing developer that stands behind it.

Let me begin with a quote out of the Early Access- Era from this game:
"...We know we aren't making any masterpiece and that's why the game is and always will have a low price."
Ok the price for the game is 3€. So i thought it is a really "cheepy and dumpy" game, i mean the most games with those prices (IF they are not some %-off) are not really in the best quallity and i more or less "know" what i will buy.
With Warriors & Castles (in short WandC now) i was not really full sure what i will buy with this low price and if the creators themself say something like i quote i only was thinking worse of it, if not even a really "bad" game.
Honestly, i played it just some rounds against bots but i had the hell of fun with it.
The Pros
-VERY very cheap price, i would even buy it for 5-8€, honestly. I guess the creators just doesnt know what they created! Its really more worth than 3€.
-Easy to understand. The game has (so far) not any tutorial but its very easy to understand if you played it a bit, its like (at least with the 3 classes i played it) a Rock-Paper-Scissors system, let me explain about without spoiler:
Warrior
- Good against Archers (coz they have pretty low health)
- Weak against Magicians (cant block the dmg full from them)
Archer
- Good against Magicians (they move pretty slow)
- Weak against Warriors (coz of the low health)
Magician
- Good against Warriors (they cant block the dmg full)
- Weak against Archers (coz of the slow movement)
- Simply "cartoony" like grafic. Really, it just fits! Its not really the "best kind" of grafic but it fits to the game and gameplay, even the splatters from blood and like
- Nothing unfair. It gives (so far) 3 classes which are well balanced and there is nothing unfair so far. Archers have limited range (magicians too), the cooldowns are good set and the building HPs are not to high set.
It also has some negativs, still...which are:
- The Animations look weird sometimes, like the characters has a "stick in the A**", if you know what i mean.
- Not really or pretty quiet "soundtrack". It really needs some good bg music if i dont use my own Heavy metal music to give the game some more "emotions" on the battlefield X3
(not really negativ but still)
- this game needs just some more "love". Really. more players, a bit more work and done. for 3€ i cant complain about that much
Fact:
WandC is a hell of fun game for such low price and i wish only it had some more players, really. The animations doesnt look so much right but i guess with some animators or some more work, the creators can still work on that. The Classes are well balanced and not "to strong" or like. If you die it is coz youre just stupit or the enemy comes in masses X3.
For 3€ its VERY good and well made, at least in the gameplay. It really just needs more players and some more "love".
I give it a 7.8/10 so far coz it really needs some more active players and maybe better animations. The rest is well made for such a low-price game!

1200 hours into this game, been playing since beta: I can only say it's one of the best Free To Play games I have ever played, period.
The gameplay is boggling, and extremely fun, especially in the early game: It'll provide you with a decent challenge for the 100 hours, assuming you don't purchase a ton of the in-game currency and bypass the grind by buying everything, instead of grinding for it. (Which is half the fun, and the central point of the game)
The biggest 'AW YEAH!' I can give this game, however, is the way it approaches the marketplace: Prime Access is kind of an insult, but the rest of the game's market is extremely healthy and alive. This is because the Developers made the decision to let players trade their 'Real Money Currency', Platinum, with each other freely. Anything that directly affects gameplay, and even MOST of the cosmetics in the game, can be received by simply grinding out items worth something to other players, and then selling them the goods in exchange for Plat. The Devs dont shove it down your throat, instead, they let the market do it's thing, and that gives much more life to the game than most give it credit for.
Thank you, DE, for a healthy economy, and allowing us to trade your premium currency. Warframe overall is a treat, and I always find myself coming back.
But.
There are a few things that could be better: 1200 hours in, I can say that I'm rather officially at the point of having broken the game in a few ways. End-game offers little challenge versus reward, Raiding is kind of a joke due to the Peer To Peer client system DE have based the game around, and the game kinda falls flat. Mind you, I got 1200 hours out of this game, and I'll probably get many more: But DE's boss design and lack of dedicated servers for big-ticket stuff, like raiding, makes the end-game experience disappointing at best, at least for me. Most raids I've ever gone into have been complete and utter messes, better reserved for a much smaller, higher skilled player count. Other players would rubberband around, and anybody you don't personally know can make the entire run fail: Just because they can't follow basic instructions.
It's about as pleasent as herding cats away from the food bowl.
PVP is also a complete and utter joke. So broken it's not even worth laughing about. The network issues glow brighter than a forest fire in the dead of night, and any 'Competitive Edge' this game had was thrown out the window when explosive weapons were allowed into the PVP modes, the Simulor especially. Expect to see people bouncing around in utterly strange, rubberbanding patterns, spamming their Simulor into nearby walls for kills. The PVP takes absolutely zero skill, and the rewards could not be farther from worth such a terrible gameplay experience.
The Early-Mid-Late game progression is great though, and you'll find yourself tinkering with builds, chomping at the bit to try new things and new styles of play, even at the very end of the game. Despite DE's shortcomings in some facets, they are shining beacons in others.
(I sure would like some heavily challenging single-player content for the end game though. Test us by our mechanical skill. Give us a reward worthy of a trial by fire.)
Overall, I can heavily recommend this game to... Everyone, really: Whether you enjoy putting together different builds in RPGs for your characters, you enjoy facing down endless waves of enemies, or if you love hitting sick shots from your rifle into a foes' weak spots. This game has something for everyone, really, and even at 1200 hours, I still have lots of fun with it.
Edit: Some fixes, new ending paragraph.
TLDR: It's basically the Witcher 3 of Free to Play. You'll enjoy it, just avoid raiding and PVP. Download this game and play it already.

I was really excited to play this game, but the more I play, the more it feels like a chore to play.
I'll cut all the crap and get to why I don't think this game is worth it
1. The combat sucks. It's a much lesser version of the Arkham style of combat. The problem with it though is that it's terribly imbalanced. Enemies love their ranged attacks, so when you're in a fight with 5+ enemies, you're constantly dodging or countering ranged attacks. Even when you can counter ranged attacks, it seems to do almost zero damage to enemies and they never die to their own arrows. Meanwhile, you're getting pounded on by 3 enemies, and you end up getting hit anyway because you can't counter the melee and ranged at the same time. So you try to dodge. And something manages to hit you while you're dodging. And things take forever to die if you didn't find a good weapon. As simple as the combat is, it's frustrating and not fun.
2. The randomness. I know it's a card game, and that's something that piqued my interest in the game, but it's too much against your favor. To unlock new cards, you have to meet prerequisites, and more often than not, you're not going to have them. But there's nothing you can do to meet them, because everything is chance. But all you want to do is unlock new cards. It's just luck. And the cards don't reward you enough. My last 3 runs were against the skeleton king, and all 3 times, I ran out of food near the end. You can only get food by chance or by buying it at randomly placed shops, but you get gold to buy things randomly and none of my cards ever gave me any gold to buy food. I never felt like my losses were my fault.
And those two faults are what make up the entire game. You only do two things: go through RNG cards and see what the results are, and fight. The RNG results aren't satisfying, and the combat isn't satisfying, so there's no sense of accomplishment. I'm really sad I don't like this game.

So full disclosure, since this game is about kinky as f*** gay sex of the female variety: Gay dude here. In normal circumstances, I'd have absolutely no interest in a game like... well, *gestures wildly* this. I have no attraction to the female form normally beyond the same way you'd appreciate a nicely decorated house, or a painting, and two women making out certainly does not turn me on.
"Wow, what an idiot", I hear you say. I don't neccessarily disagree with you there. But despite on the surface not being the target market for the game, I actually really appreciated my time with Ladykiller in a Bind. Sex is a huge part of Ladykiller, and if you're uncomfortable with that I'm just going to say that the game's probably not for you, but it's not big solely in a fanservice way. It's also about the characters, and power dynamics, and consent. (Also there's a christmas jumper mode if you don't like the idea of seeing a bunch of naked women. It's what it sounds like. There's also an option to skip the sex scenes, but for THE MOST PART I'd recommend not using it.)
In terms of the gameplay, it's a surprisingly interactive visual novel. Normally, when you have a conversation in a game, the characters say their bit, and then control is handed to the player as they're asked "Do you want to kick the puppy, yes or no".  Not so in Ladykiller. Instead, dialogue options pop into (and out of) the main character's head as you progress through the conversation, which makes the actual act of choosing options seem a lot less stilted. It's not perfect mind you, occasionally if you wait to click on a dialogue option then it's pretty clear that it's best read as an immediate follow up to a line from a while ago, but as it stands it's a major improvement compared to the other visual novels I've read.
The music and art is also worth mentioning. Whilst the tracks themselves are pretty good in of themselves, what *did* stand out was the fact that the music dynamically changes to match who's in the conversation, how kinky the sex is getting, etc., which was pretty neat. Similarly, the art is pretty good, but the standout part is the fact that everyone has multiple outfits, there's plenty of cgs, and I really like the colours used generally throughout. Good stuff.
Plot wise - I'll be honest, by itself the overarching plot is not particularly interesting. You can play multiple times to learn more about what's going on, but it's not developed that much and when it was I wasn't super interested. Fortunately, this is because it largely comes across as an excuse to get to the actual meat of the story: A woman pretending to be her brother as she makes out with a bunch of other women. The dialogue is often hilarious, the characters are interesting, and it's fun trying to be as flirtateous as possible without coming across as suspicious. For the 90% of the game that this sort of thing is happening, I had a great time.

Hard Reset is an intense first-person shooter that takes place in a futuristic cyberpunk envoirnment and city. To play it, you're going to want at least three things: A desire to shoot countless hordes of robots, patience of iron, and a pretty powerful graphics card. If you don't have one or more of these things, Hard Reset probably isn't for you.
This game has a really awesome art style, both the beautiful enviornments that you play in, and the cutscenes that play at the beginning of a level. The cutscenes themselves play like a sci-fi comic book, which I think is really neat, though most of the time it doesn't feel like there's much story involved. The gameplay itself is oldschool right down to the bare bones, sort of a hybrid of painkiller, doom and serious sam. You'll engage in plenty of hardcore combat with all sorts of robots that appear throughout the levels and try to kill them by any means necessary, whether it be mowing them down with your weapons, or blowing up enviornmental hazards around them, ranging from barrels, electrical machines, cars...you get the idea.
Probably one of the coolest features of Hard Reset is that, unlike most oldschool shooters, you don't actually collect new guns. Instead, you get to power up the weapons and gear the game starts you out with by collecting Nanos, then going to upgrade machines to select the upgrades you desire. For example, you can upgrade your assault rifle to be things like a shotgun and an rpg, and you can improve the quality of your armor and health, to name a few things. Nanos can be collected by killing enemies, looking throughout the levels, and finding secrets by looking high and low for them and blowing up walls.
Even though I really like Hard Reset, I'll admit it's not for everyone---it can get rather frustrating at times, since enemies often appear in swarms really quickly and can often result in stupid deaths (though to be fair, I AM playing on insane difficulty), and the game does have very little story (mostly just kill machines and complete objectives). Very highly recommended for those who love intense oldschool gameplay and cyberpunk/sci-fi games, though. 3.5/5.0

This game presents itself as "a tribute to old-school shooters". Indeed, it has some specifics from earlier times such as non-regenerating health (shields regenerate though), health and ammo pickups, secrets and waves upon waves of enemies. However, developers must have thought that "old-school=hardcore" and this game suffers from several major drawbacks.
- no quicksave. actually, no save at all. game uses autosave functions whenever it thinks is the best time
- story is some mess
- bulletsponged enemies. even on normal the weakest enemies require to waste your ammo
- practically all enemies use the same tactics - to jump on you or to charge at you and deal melee damage
- if you manage to hide, than you will be damaged by homing ranged attacks
- if you try to "head-to-head" fight, your only way to defend yourself is sidestepping. But guess what? You move VEEERYYY slowly, all enemies are much faster than you
- lackluster guns. out of all 10 weapon upgrades, 2 or 3 are capable of dealing at least some sort of damage: RPG. Grenade launcher, Railgun and for the best - Smartgun. You will spam smartgun 99% of the time when you get it.
- Lackluster guns make you too much dependable on environmental damage
- slow and clunky movement and jumping makes finding some secrets very frustrating. it is unknown whether you can't reach some places because there is an invisible wall or because your jumping sucks. Not to mention jump-stepping, when you wand, you automatically step forward or sideways
- ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥eeet boss battles, especially that sucker from the Exile DLC.
- all these drawbacks make Hard Reset a really hard game (thus probably the name, it resets you brain)
The positive points are:
+ Nice graphics and art
+ Interesting evolving weapons (similar to Bioshock)
+ It is not "a modern realistic military shooter"
In the end, I would recommend this game for those who want a challenging scifi shooter that puts you in a disadvantage all the time. If you just want to kill waves of enemies, play Serious Sam instead.

Story:
In an alternate universe Europe is undergoing WWII due to a lack of a multipurpose energy resource called ragnite. The neutral country Gallia is invaded by the Empire for its rich ragnite resources
. The main characters, Welkin and Alicia, end up leading Squad 7 and take part in various military campaigns. As the war goes on the true motives for the Empire's invasion are revealed.
The story is told through episodes. Some of them you play and some you just watch. It is kind of like an anime and there are even filler episodes you can buy responsibly with your military funds, one of which is the anime required beach episode. You can rewatch episodes but you cannot replay campaigns. The only campaigns you can replay are the bonus skirmishes, most of which resemble the actual campaign you played.
Gameplay:
This is a turn based RPG, however you have full control of your character (a unit of your squad) and can aim with them too. There are 6 classes: Scout, Shocktrooper, Lancer, Engineer, Sniper, and Tank Commander. Scouts can move the farthest in one turn and spot enemies more easily than other classes, they have a weak but accurate gun and their defense is low. Shocktroopers can move a low to medium amount in one turn, their defense is good and they can carry a powerful machine gun and flamethrower. Lancers cannot move very far but they are effective against tanks. I believe they can also get a variant of their weapon that makes their lances (rocket launchers) have a wider spread for groups of enemies. Engineers can refill ammo and repair guard towers, sandbags, and tanks. They can heal more effectively too. Snipers cannot move very far and have low defense. In the first half of the game they are pretty much useless because they will ALWAYS miss. Later on you can upgrade your sniper rifle with Aim stat A and they will be pretty useful then. Tank Commanders will always be in their tanks. You will get 2 tanks in the game but in the first half you can only control 1. Tanks can kill other tanks and groups of soldiers and they can break down barricades. You can also use it as a shield for your troops in the back and you get smoke rounds later on.
Although you can aim in this game it does have random elements (RNG). Most enemies will die when you shoot them in the head with a shocktrooper or scout but some will dodge randomly. Lancers and Snipers will frequently miss even on later stages when you have your weapons upgraded. It is not too big of a downer but on the last stage you might have to shoot an armored enemy and they only shot the target 1 out of 4 times. That is 3 turns wasted. Tanks can also shoot armored enemies but they take 2 CP (turns) rather than 1 CP. I said "might" because there is a chance that the boss won't activate those armored enemies (another random element). On a reload he did not and I was able to finish the boss on that turn.
You level up and purchase upgrades for the entire class rather than individual characters. In my opinion I love that feature because you can play the game without too much fuss. YYour squad members can die but you can save them if you get to them in less than 3 turns, complete the mission or reload a save from before. But you get an achievement the first time one of them dies so I was OK after one of mine died. The princess even gives you an award. Joking aside it was kind of sad when my squad member Coby died because they each have their own story and personality shown by their dialogue and unique abilities. Some characters unique abilities and they like certain people. When they are by a person they like (as a friend or love) they get status up. I believe status up makes them less likely to miss or raises their defense. I am not too sure. The character like system doesn't really get in the way of the game but it would help those that wish to use it. Each class also has certain abilities that are unlocked as you level up in addition to the unique ones. While some unique abilities simply give them a status up others change the gameplay. One unique ability, "Hard Worker", allows the character to shoot again. Another one allows you to instantly heal. Certain class abilities can increase damage, or allow better tank repairs. There are some bad abilities too. One called "Moody" prevents you from doing anything on your turn. Some characters are also racist or sexist and will get a status down by the type of person they hate, including Darcsens, women or men.
This is a fun great game and it really is fun planning your moves. The ability to move your character and aim with them is a plus. I only like RPGs if they allow you to control your character in some way, like Mario & Luigi. There is even a New Game Plus. This is definitely a buy.
Like RPGs? Get this game! Interesting characters and storylines, as well as fun turn-based action.

In Murdered Soul Suspect, you play an ex-con detective who was thrown through a 4th story window and shot to death. Your ghost haunts the streets of Salem, Mass and you must solve your own murder before the night is over.
The tone is really nice here. There's a lot of influence from early Puritan Salem in the architecture and ghostly relics and fellow ghosts in need of a detective add some light side quests. The tone is similar to the Ghostbusters game, but without the ghostbusters.
The puzzle solving gameplay is really nice, but the rest of it is lacking.
The story itself is good, but the game makes a few stupid choices to guide you between mystery pieces. Aside from investigation and walking around, you'll have to defeat demon ghosts (by sneaking up behind them) and help a human stealth around by walking up to electronic objects and pressing buttons. These sections feel really weak in an otherwise well put together game, partially because you're already a ghost and therefore any attempt to build tension or threaten the player falls by the wayside.

The lore and story telling is pretty nice and can entertian a single person as you go through each race's storyline but the way it's set up does not lend itself well to bringing friends into the game as quests are handled on an almost exclusively single player basis early on.All the early quests are pretty standard "kill this many things and collect pieces", "go to this place and talk to this person", and "go do this thing that will teach you how to use this game feature".  The quests do, however, have a really nice feature I wish more MMOs would implement and that is that you can complete a quest early or overachive a quest with a trade off of either less time spent doing a quest or better rewards (a rarer upgraded version of the reward gear usually)
Early Multiplayer experience (PvE):
Eventually you will gain access to multiplayer dungeons and occasionally world bosses which is a bit more multiplayer friendly by nature and it will kind of require you to get some friends unless you are a straight up combat focused class.  Higher level players seem to be rewarded for "mentoring" lower level players through dungeons though I have yet to get the details on this.  It seems to be enough of a reward (or possibly a requirment) that higher level players will sometimes actively look for lower level players to "mentor".
PvP:
I have very little knowledge of this aspect though there are a number of people claiming it is "pay2win" and with the cash shop items and specail paid bonuses I've seen, I can believe it.  Back when this game first released I bought a special pack (which was late to get mailed to me among other issues which drove me away from the game early on).  In the pack, I got a bunch of crafting materials, extra bonus potions for leveling and other stat buffs, and a title which gave me a permenant stat buff to a few stats limited to only those who bought it.  This implies that there are some very specific buffs that I'm not sure you CAN get as a free player which may help give you an edge in combat.  Pay 2 win indeed.
There are duels and a bloodlust mode that allows you to attack players of the same faction though jail time for doing it seems to make it less of a problem than it could be.  The two main nations are also at war with two races per nation and a territory capture system that you will occasionally see notifications for in the chat.  There is also glider and sea ship combat which I have not really tested out but the glider combat seems to be more of a gimmick than a truly decisive factor.  Ship combat does seem a little important as cargo ships could potentially be a good source of trade money.
Crafting, trading, and the economy:
The crafting system seems to be complex and rely heavily on both gathering materials in the wild and growing them yourself in either public land (which allows people to steal them without penalty if I recall correctly) or on private land which seem that you have to pay money to become a patron to actually own any land.  I think trade also provides some needed materials from places that can only be gained from distant areas from each other.
The auction seems to be availible to patrons for a much discounted price which gives them a little more of a monopoly over the economy but I believe free players can at least participate in this.
Most things in this require labor points which you gain 5 points of per 5 minutes online as a free player and double that as a patron player with the 5 points per 5 minutes happening while the patron player is offline.  The patrons also get 5000 labor points maximum while a free player gets 2000. Labor points run out quickly due to the fact that they are needed for almost every form of advancment in the game whether it's opening the coin purses of fallen enemies, breaking things down into materials or putting them together into usuable objects.  You will need them and they will be painfully slow to come back once you've lost them.  You may find yourself idling in an area until your labor points recover enough to craft things or even just to get a hold of the money and exp that's taking up space in your inventory slots as purses and bags.
OK, but do you recommend this?:
Well... yes and no...
NO:
You will not want to stick around unless you plan on throwing money at the game and it may be a better use of money to spend on a game like Black Desert Online anyway.  The economy, PvP, and even a little bit of the PvE is rigged for patron (paying) players to the point that you might as well call it a subscription based game with free to play players acting as filler.  A free to play player is, point blank, a second class citizen in this game, as much as the main story tries to play you up to be the hero, there is little else than playing second fiddle to paid players left for you once you are done questing.
YES:
That being said, if all you are there for IS the questing, then you are in for a treat.  The storylines, I've found, are well made and the world is rich in lore, cenimatic cutscenes, and voiced stories of "your" adventure throughout the main quest line.  Many of the side quests tie in quite well to the main quest line and you can often overachieve to get gear that feels just a little bit more special than the gear you would get normally.  I personally really like questing, even if it is geared towards a single player more often than not.  If you find that you can stand the way the economy system is stacked against you, then more power to you but I feel that after that you finish the quests, the game will likely have nothing else to offer a free to play player but by all means, it is free to play.  Try it out and see for yourself.

Recettear....an adorable little RPG that doesn't take itself too seriously, because it doesn't need to. While it may be short, with a story mode easily completed in 4-6 hours, there is a surprising amount of depth for those who seek it.
For completionists, the main goal is to complete the item encyclopedia, which seems simple enough...however, even after a playthrough of the story mode, you may only be left with <25% completion, especially if you never went through the dungeon. You may have also missed many cutscenes, and missed several potential unlocks. Luckily, the game provides an endless mode for you to clean up any loose ends, and start going towards that 100%!
Pros
-cute art style
-Dialogue is well-written, with many subtle jokes and references you may not get your first way through.
-Recette and Tear are a very likeable pair, and they all have unique reactions to other characters.
-Surprising amount of depth, with dungeoneering, crafting, and a small meta game of equipping your adventurers with the best gear.
-Simple, yet effective game mechanics
-Soundtrack is nice
-Offers a fair amount of post-story content, including an endless mode (continue playing without having to worry about debts), New Game+ (With new content. Start over from day 1 with levels and items intact and repay the debt again) and survival mode (where you have to keep paying back the debt, and see how long you can last).
Cons
-Art style, especially in dungeons, can be inconsistent. Some mobs are 3d, while your player characters are always 2d sprites.
-Game will either be extremely easy to get through, or RNG will doom you into a situation where you are failing to pay off your debts
-You don't need to do any dungeon'ing or crafting to complete story mode
-Time management can be a bit troublesome, since going through dungeons requires you to give up almost an entire day in your schedule.
-Small frustrating issues, such as being unable to see outstanding orders without speaking to Tear in the shop. (If you leave to go purchase wares, you lose a share of time, and you can only double check what items you need by returning and wasting another share.)
-Dungeon combat is pretty simple, and can be very grindy
Neutral
-Game lies to you, and fails to tell you about important game mechanics. (do NOT sell for 130% base price)
-Why are you selling knives to children...?
-New Game+ is incredibly easy. The amount you must pay never increases.
Overall I actually really like Recettear. It's cute, enjoyable, and can certainly be stressful sometimes. There are a few issues, such as major game mechanics being more risk than reward during the story mode. Still, I would recommend this game not only because it provides for a surprisingly absent genre of game (running an RPG store), but it provides it in such a way that is very appealing and cheerful.

I really want people to play this game! It's a cute idea that seems like a blast to play with friends. However, the game needs more people playing it. If you're on the fence about buying it, here is what you should know:
Pros:
-Cheap! Game is a steal honestly. Its not at its peak value yet because of the small playerbase, but it's a tiny investment.
-Simple concept. Gets the job done with streamlined gameplay that really gets to the core of class based "shooter." Doesn't really fit that title much, but its more akin to TF2 than other games.
-Quick rounds! Doesn't take long to play honestly which is great! Haven't played with people yet but should be a blast with friends!
Cons:
-Game simply doesn't look all that nice. This helps gameplay by simplifying interactions with very little clutter and helps keep the game running smoothly on any machine, but be warned, it doesn't look any better playing than the screenshots do.
-Poorly optimized. Even though it plays well on any machine, the game is more sluggish than a well optimized AAA game or even most indie games. Early access does mean some of this is expected.
-No players. This might bug potential buyers more than it should because the AI isn't exactly great, but buying this game helps in this regard!
Add me if you want to play, this game is cute and cheap and frankly I think its a good example of what an amateur early access title should look like.

Okay I made a big blog post about this game months ago, so I'll post the link here and give you guys a rundown of what I think:
1. I love Christine Love's work very much. I think the UI and choice system is incredible and should set the new industry standard in visual novels.
2. There's something weird going on with Raide's art in this game. I wonder if he was driven out of his comfort zone?
3. The music and the way the music interacts with the story is incredible.
4. Christine uses a lot of interesting themes to motivate the overarching plot of Ladykiller. Unfortunately, they do not all mesh or manifest the way they were intended. The themes of consent and manipulation are not followed through entirely, and if you're not fully prepared for the harem ending, you WILL end up forced to endure a dub-con scene to get to the end. <--I guess this was patched out. But why wasn't it it there to begin with?
I don't hate Ladykiller, but my feelings on it have been very mixed. I've fallen into the void where disappointment in a work makes it hard for me to remember this game fondly. I don't think it's horrible. I think it is worth playing. I can't give it a harsh 5/10 on steam, so I will not recommend it.
(Sorry Christine. I love you and your work very much.)

This is one of those games that test your mental strength and finger dexterity. Games which gives me similar experiences are Dark Souls & Legend Of Korra. I will relate my personal experience. In story mode, which is the awesome part of the game, you will encounter the bosses, Jacks/Queens/Kings of the 4 suits (Dust, Skulls, Plague, Scales) The first 6 bosses (jacks & some queens) are easy, then you get to the 7th boss, and you start dying more & more frequently, that's where the game starts to push you to your limit. Initially I love combat & its rewards, i say "Bring It On!", but now on, i say "Damn It, Too Risky. I've already gone so far". To get to the boss is already a challenge, if you are greedy. Since the rolls are not entirely about luck, you can track the positions of the "Success" cards, if your eyes are fast enough. This makes u bolder but complacent.
I have 1 run which I got to the King Of Plague without any good weapon except a rusty axe (penniless, hungry, wounded & unlucky), and I know I am screwed. But lo & behold, i freaking killed him with 7hp left, I cant believe it!
I have 1 run which i failed in the vampire roll and got sucked to 1hp, and i said "f*** it, i should restart" and try to find a way to suicide, but I dont know how I just survived encounter after encounter, eventually went on to pick up a good weapon & killed King Of Skulls, where all my other "normal" runs failed, the hell...
To sum it up, sometimes I freaking dont know how I did it, its like a rollercoaster ride. "From light comes darkness, and from darkness comes light". Thank you for the experience which I will remember for life.

Keep in mind, this is a review written immediately after playing the game ONCE, and my opinions may change after experiencing different choice sets.  I will update this later.
OVERALL: I liked this game and would recommend it to people who enjoy visual novels with self-awareness and humor.  There needs to be more visual novels that're worth playing and replaying, and this is one of those from the looks of it.  The achievements imply some very different endings that are truly based on your decisions throughout the game, and it certainly looks like the ending I got was tailored to the choices I'd made throughout mine.  I'm certainly going to be playing it a few more times through.
PROS: Entertaining writing, characters that fit the mood and theme of the story, and the surprises at the end of the game as things begin to wrap up.  I was also very pleased with certain characters especially, such as The Bro, and how the BDSM side of things was handled with The Beauty.
CONS:
There are definitely cringe-worthy moments throughout the game that I don't think were intended to be cringy, such as implying that everyone in Kentucky is racist (?) and some other, uh, delightful moments of speech like that (like how one person could only say something they did because they were white...yikes).  On the other hand, these are Canadians, and I've known a lot of Canadians who actually talk the way this game does, so it's realistic as far as the ridiculously PC-level discussion sometimes goes.  Sometimes it just sounds like the characters being themselves; sometimes it sounds...really awkward and takes the reader out of the scene.  To each their own, however - some of it is well-done, others not.  Overall, I like the writing, just not those parts.
I'm probably just boring, but I wasn't really fond of how sex came across as cheap, easy and...just, the ease in which certain people agreed to sharing was distressing.  Still, that's a personal preference, not a real negative to the writing itself.  Some people will love the game that much more for it, and the game never hides what it's doing.  The honesty of the characters just enjoying themselves is refreshing; the easy acceptance of people clearly sexing each other up without discussing it with prior established relations, not so much.

Gateway To Gaming Presents:
Ladykiller in a Bind, A Visual Novel Review
Disclosure: This visual novel was bought by the review.
Visual Novel experience: Muv-Luv Alternative, Kindred Spirits on the Roof, Danganronpa: Trigger Happy Havoc, VA-11 Hall-A: Cyberpunk Bartender Action
Please note: I will try to keep this as spoiler free as possible. If you are interested in spoilers, I don't mind explaining in detail with a link to a separate group.
The visual aesthetic's quality is a mixed bag, but nothing dips beneath terrible. The backgrounds and environmental set pieces are absolutely beautiful to look at, ranging from the hallways of the cruise ship to the dinning facility and pool tables located in the lounge. Random pieces of art are also included via the third epilogue, which had a couple of noteworthy pieces done in black and white shading. The UI and the option menu are all presented cleanly and in uniform fashion, something I wish a lot of other visual novels could mimic. In terms of the sexual content in this game, it is very tame with simply drawn genitalia (nothing detailed) and the most extreme act being penetration. It is nothing to write home about and due to some serious story issues, feels more tacked on than genuine. Yes, BDSM is also featured, but the use of the crop is never shown, just emphasized by sound effects.
Character avatars are shown during conversation to help specify who is talking, but they are all rather similar in terms of build and height. The main menu screen illustrates this best, having each character side by side with their outfits and hair being the only real feature separating them. Faces, unfortunately, also suffer the exact same issue most visuals novels have when dealing with their characters. The faces are interchangeable with no definition to the way noses look and provide the strange case of "same face, different hair style and eye color. It just feels lazy, a feature that can easily be fixed by giving the time to provide cheek definition. This makes the characters look sterile, clean cut and bland. Thankfully, much more care was given to the outfits that range from spectacular (looking at your wardrobe Boss) to simply quaint. Clothing wrinkles and stretch lines were sown into most poses as well. The game actually uses multiple poses, different angles for each character that helps convey emotion over simply having the assumption from a single avatar. If it wasn't for the faces though, I probably would have given the character artwork a plus.
Music, I am pleased to announce, was mellow throughout and never seemed to outstay its' welcome during the short duration of conversations. During times of tension, the tempo picks up and helps carry some scenes that otherwise fall flat from delivered dialog. It is by no means terrible, but once I finished the game for the third time, I honestly couldn't remember any of the melodies used. It would also help if the main menu could feature at least some form of music. Sound effects are minor, mostly given to the pounding of waves against the hull and the swift cracks of the crop. The only major omission from this visual novel is voice acting, which again, leaves the music to help carry scenes. Granted, the developer's other games lacked voice talent, but they were also not $30 dollars.
Conversations play a major role in the manipulation game, influencing the way the story progress in regards to the individual classmates. While the main story follows the same script, the player can choose to interact with specific people at special times of the day, adding the chance to garner more votes while trying to avoid triggering suspicion. Each character has dialog paths that can unlock sentences worth of different text and others that are needed to progress down the path to either a peaceful resolution, breaking it off in poor taste or commemorating friendship on silk sheets. Certain conversation options are also blocked that can only be unlocked if certain interactions occur to gain information regarding that character. Options can also open up or disappear depending on how long you continue to listen to a conversation, which can be beneficial or harmful. Honestly, if the player goes to far into a conversation, they can roll back up using the mouse wheel and select a less impactful option in most cases. How can someone tell? Every dialog option has their profits and losses written next too it, which makes deciding on a specific path incredible easy. It also removes any real danger of rousing suspicion (except for one unavoidable situation) and makes the conversations less enjoyable. It is a great system (in terms of removing options) dragged down by unnecessary hand holding and a lack of discoverability.
The game also handles the idea of a fail-state poorly. If a player somehow manages to get five suspicion points, the game cuts to the same conversation, the same outcome, then uses the unreliable narrator to reload the same time of day for a retry. This was a missed opportunity to examine the reactions that would have been made, leading to more potential endings and uses of the manipulation narrative. It all feels too "safe" in a genre that has given some very amazing story arcs during what equates to a game over. It boils down to a missed opportunity in a disappointing story.
Story-wise, this is a mess of a title. This is without taking into account the dialog, the character motivations, the general lack of chemistry and the themes used by the developer (which are all subjective). It takes at least three play-throughs to get all the information needed to understand the main plot and goes from out of left field to incredibly outlandish for what was advertised as a simple story about high school romance and votes. The cruise is simply an excuse to set up the protagonist for the ending and doesn't involve any of the classmates plot wise, which makes the cruise seem more like filler except for the interaction with The Stalker and The Beauty (who wipes away your suspicion points if you decide to submit to her). It is hard to really pin point the issue without spoilers, so I will try it this way: this is two visual novels wrapped into one, with the first being a "fish out of water" romance comedy and the second being an origin story to a Call of Duty villain. That is how disjointed and out of place the ending feels, which would have probably just been a good place to start the planned sequel for this game.
The core premise also takes a nose dive off the plot-line close to the end as it is revealed the need for votes is arbitrary, resulting in the same ending regardless of how many are acquired. On a side note: votes are needed to unlock certain paths during Day 6 for individual characters, not the main plot. It doesn't help that the chemistry introduced is paper thin (for the actual brother, not the sister). The reason for adding the consequences for certain dialog options was made to help play off the brother, I understand this, but there is barely any relationship or motivations revealed outside "he is my rival" or "I use to date her." If there were more details involving situations like the unavoidable conundrum I mentioned early, it might have been needed. The characters just don't have a well written history to give off or promoted angles to make them anything but one dimensional.
Technical issues are also present on this little lust boat. Crashes have occurred three times during my play-throughs, once for hitting New Game and twice while loading two separate saves. Dialog also has a tendency to repeat itself, as if the scene was meant to be a placeholder for the finished sentence. Music would something play while I was reading something, cut off while I was reading that same page, then start again before clicking to the next page.
